children.translated_text: '<s>Utprāsana</s>' means the full comprehension of the intended meaning.

children.text: atra prathamārjunabhīmaśabdau vācyaparau, caramau tu vyaṅgyaparau /
children.translated_text: Here, the first uses of the words '<s>Arjuna</s>' and '<s>Bhīma</s>' pertain to the denoted meaning, while the latter ones pertain to the suggested meaning.
The conjunction of contradictory properties serves to exclude an equal counterpart.
Therefore, because of the absence of correlation with another such entity, this becomes <s>ananvaya</s> (non-correlation).

body.translated_text: Now, how can the status of <s>upameya</s> and <s>upamāna</s> coexist in one and the same thing?—to address this he says '<s>vācyābhiprāyeṇa</s>' etc. The prior form is the <s>upameya</s>-hood; its conformity is from the standpoint of the denoted (<s>vācya</s>). The unprecedented form is the <s>upamāna</s>-hood; its conformity is from the standpoint of the suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>)—such is the purport. Now, what is the purpose obtained through the conjunction of contradictory properties in one thing?—to address this he says '<s>ekasya tu viruddha</s>' etc.

body.text: atha tṛtīyasabrahmacārinivṛttiphalīmupameyopamāṃ sūtrayati-
body.translated_text: Now he formulates the sūtra on <s>upameyopamā</s> (mutual simile), which has the result of excluding a third associate—

body.text: dvayoḥ paryāyeṇa tasminnupameyopamā || 13 ||
body.translated_text: When the two reciprocally [exchange the roles of upamāna and upameya], that is <s>upameyopamā</s>. (RuAss 13)

body.text:
dvayorupamānopameyabhāvavinimaye satyupameyopamālaṅkāra ityarthaḥ /
tadetadvyācaṣṭe-tacchabdenetyādi /
tacchabdenopamānopameyatvapratyavamarśa iti vadatā sannihitānanvayapratyavamarśaśaṅkā nivāryate /
ananvayādvaidharmyāntaraṃ darśayitumāha-paryāya ityādi /
yaugapadyamihaikavākyānupraveśaḥ /
tadabhāvādbhinnavākyatvamevetyāha-ataivatviti /
atrāyamāśayaḥ /
upameyamuddeśyam, upamānaṃ tu vidheyam /
itthaṃ ca satyupamānopameyabhāvavyatyayo vākyaikavākyatāmantareṇa na saṃbhavati /
ananvaye tu padaikavākyataiveti /
atra bimbapratibimbabhāvo na saṃbhavati /
bhinnavākyatvena tannibandhanavaicitryapratīteḥ /
sādharmyanibandhanamanyat /
vaicitryadvayaṃ saṃbhavatītyāha-iyaṃ tu dharmasyetyādi /
sādhāraṇyamaikyarūpyeṇa nirdeśaḥ /
vastuprativastubhāvastu pratītacaraḥ /
khamiveti /
atra pratīyamānasya nairmalyadharmasyānugāmitvena sādhāraṇyam /

children.translated_text: '<s>Sacchāya</s>'—thus.
'<s>Chāyā</s>' means radiance; here the quality of having radiance is differentiated due to the difference of the related entities.
The exchange of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> status is not possible without sequence.
Therefore <s>upameyopamā</s> pertains to the domain of separate sentences.

body.translated_text: When there is an interchange of the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship between the two, that is the figure of <s>upameyopamā</s>—such is the meaning. He explains this: '<s>tacchabdena</s>' etc. By saying 'the recognition of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> status by means of the word "<s>tad</s>",' the apprehension of the proximate <s>ananvaya</s> is excluded. To show the further distinction from <s>ananvaya</s>, he says '<s>paryāya</s>' etc. Simultaneity here means inclusion within a single sentence. In the absence of that—

body.text: atha smaraṇaṃ sūtrayati-
body.translated_text: Now he formulates the sūtra on <s>smaraṇa</s> (remembrance)—

body.text: sadṛśānubhāvādvastvantarasmṛtiḥ smaraṇam || 14 ||
body.translated_text: The recollection of another thing due to the experience of something similar is <s>smaraṇa</s> (remembrance). (RuAss 14)

body.text:
sadṛśānubhavāt sadṛśāntarasmaraṇaṃ smraṇālaṅkāraḥ /
vyācaṣṭe-vastvantaramiti /
sadṛśaṃ samabhivyāhārādvastvantarasadṛśameveti bhāvaḥ /
dviṣṭhasya dharmasya ekatra sthāsnoḥ pratiyogyapekṣāmantareṇa anuparamādanumānavairmyāyāha-avanābhāvetyādi /
avinābhāvo vyātpiḥ /
nahi gavādidarśane niyamena gavayādisadṛśāntarasmaraṇamasti /
tādātmyavadutpattyoranyatarābhāvenāliṅgatvāt /
atiśayiteti /
iyaṃ yoddhukāmaṃ lavamālokya sakautukasya sūtasya candraketuṃ pratyuktiḥ /
tadaiva tulyarūpamiti sadṛśānubhāvodgaghāṭanam /
asādṛśyahetukā smṛtirnasmaraṇālaṅkāra ityāha-sādṛśyaṃ vinā tviti /
pratyudāharati-atrānugodamiti /
atra hi pūrvānubhūtārthadarśanādeva smṛtiḥ na tu sadṛśānubhavāt /
prasaṅgāt gūḍhamabhavanmatayogadoṣamudghāṭayati-atra ca kartṛviśeṣaṇānāmityādi /
mṛgayādaśābhāvikartṛviśeṣaṇānāṃ smarāmīti smaraṇakriyākartṛrdāśaratherviśeṣaṇānāṃ mṛgayanivṛttyādīnāṃ smartavyadaśābhāvitve 'nubhūtacaratvāt /
smartavyamṛgayādaśabhāvitve yukte smartṛdaśābhāvitvaṃ mṛgayānivṛttiṃsmarāmīti smaraṇakālabhāvitvamasamīcīnam /
nahi mṛgayānivṛttyapanītakhedatvādiviśiṣṭasmṛtiḥ /
kintu mṛgayānivṛttyādikaṃ smartavyasutpiviśeṣaṇamata iṣṭārtho 'pi na bhavatītyabhavanmatayogākhyo 'yaṃ doṣaḥ /
nanu yadi preyo 'laṅkāro ratibhāvātmakaḥ, na tadā smṛtiḥ /
yadā tu vyabhicāribhāvātmakastadā smṛtirūpo 'pi kadācitsaṃbhavati /
tato 'sya smaraṇālaṅkārasya kiṃ vaidharmyamityata āha-preyo 'saṅkārāsya tvityādi /
udāhṛtya darśayati-aho kope 'pi kāntaṃ mukhamityādi /
atrābhiniviṣṭasya nāyakasya priyānurāgasaṃskārāṇāṃ saskārāntarābhibhāva katayābhūyobhūyaḥsamuddhudhyamānānāṃ mahimnaiva smṛtiḥ, nahi sadṛśānubhāvāt /
vaidharmyāntaramuddhāvayati-tatrāpi vibhāvetyādi /
vibhāvānubhāvādibhiḥ yadā smṛtirvyajyate, tadaiva hi bhāvālaṅkāraḥ /
yairdṛṣṭo 'sīti /
prāsaprahāranetrayorasṛkstrutyanalajvālayoḥ parapātanakāladahanayoḥ nāyakasmararipvośca sādṛśyaṃ vivakṣyate /
atra yo 'yaṃ sadṛśavastvantarānubhāvoyairdṛṣṭo 'sīti nirdiṣṭaḥ /
nāsau smararipusmaraṇajananātsmaraṇālaṅkāraḥ kintvaśakyasmararipudarśanakautukāstamayarūpārthāntarakaraṇātmā viśeṣālaṅkāraḥ /
etaddarśanena tadapi siddhamiti pratīteḥ /
nanvaśakyavastvantarakaraṇaṃ viśeṣālaṅkārasya lakṣaṇaṃ, iha tu karaṇaṃ nopalabhāmaha ityata āha-karaṇāsyetyādi /

children.text: kṛñbhvastyarthānāṃ sarvadhātvanuyāyitvāt kriyāyāḥsāmānyātmā karotyarthaḥ darśane 'pi saṃbhavata /
children.translated_text: Since the meanings of [the verbal roots] <s>kṛ</s> (to do/make), <s>bhū</s> (to be/become), and <s>as</s> (to exist) follow all verbal roots, the meaning of '<s>karoti</s>' (makes/produces) — being the generic form of action — is possible even in [the context of] 'seeing.'
As has been stated by us in the <s>Prayogadīpikā</s>:
'Those verbal roots whose agents are indifferent are to be known as having the meaning of <s>asti</s> (existence);
those whose agents undergo transformation have the meaning of <s>bhū</s> (becoming); and those whose agents employ [actively] have the meaning of <s>kṛ</s> (making).'

body.translated_text: The remembrance of something similar from a similar experience is the figure of <s>Smaraṇa</s> (Remembrance). He explains: '<s>Vastvantaram</s>' (another object) — [it means] another object similar [to the present one], as implied by the [surrounding] context. To show that, without regard to the counterpart, the invariable property residing in one locus does not remain without the other — [thereby showing it is] different from inference — he says: 'In the absence of invariable concomitance (<s>Avinābhāva</s>),' and so on. <s>Avinābhāva</s> means invariable co-presence (<s>Vyāpti</s>). For upon seeing a cow and such, there is not necessarily a remembrance of a similar thing like a <s>Gavaya</s> (wild ox). Because, due to the absence of either essential identity (<s>Tādātmya</s>) or origination (<s>Vadutpatti</s>), it is not a valid inferential mark. '<s>Atiśayita</s>' (surpassing): this is the reply of the charioteer, who is filled with curiosity upon seeing <s>Lava</s> eager to fight, addressed to <s>Candraketu</s>. 'Of the same appearance then' — this is the indication of the experience of similarity. Memory caused by dissimilarity is not the figure of <s>Smaraṇa</s> — he says: 'But without similarity.' He gives a counter-example: 'Here, <s>Anugoda</s>.' For here, the memory arises from seeing a previously experienced object, not from the experience of a similar [but different] object. In passing, he exposes a hidden flaw in a certain [commentator's] view — [the flaw called] <s>Abhavanmatayoga</s> (attribution of a state to an inappropriate bearer) — saying: 'And here, of the qualifiers of the agent,' and so on. The qualifiers of the agent — the states [characterizing] the hunting episode — belong to the agent of the act of remembering, namely <s>Dāśaratha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>). The states of the hunting-cessation and similar [activities], because they existed as experienced [by the rememberer], properly belong to the state of what is to be remembered. When properly [understood] as states belonging to the object to be remembered (the hunting episode), the attribution of the state of the remembering-time to the rememberer — [such as] 'I remember the cessation of the hunt' — is inappropriate. For the memory is not qualified by the cessation-of-hunting-dispelled-weariness and such; rather, the cessation of hunting and such are qualifiers of what is to be remembered. Therefore even the intended meaning does not result — this flaw is called <s>Abhavanmatayogadoṣa</s> (attribution of a state to an improper locus). Now, if the figure <s>Preyas</s> (the Dear) has the nature of the <s>Bhāva</s> of <s>Rati</s> (love), then it is not memory. But when it has the nature of a <s>Vyabhicāribhāva</s> (transitory emotion), then sometimes it may take the form of memory. Then what is the distinguishing characteristic of this <s>Smaraṇālaṅkāra</s>? — to this he says: 'Of <s>Preyas</s>, however,' and so on. He illustrates with an example: 'Ah, even in anger, the beloved face,' and so on. Here, the <s>Saṃskāras</s> (impressions) of the hero's love for his beloved, which are repeatedly revived due to the suppression of other impressions — memory [arises] from the sheer force of those [impressions], not from the experience of a similar object. He draws out another distinguishing feature: 'There too, through <s>Vibhāvas</s> (determinants),' and so on. When memory is suggested through <s>Vibhāvas</s>, <s>Anubhāvas</s> (consequents), and other [elements], only then is it the figure of <s>Bhāva</s> (Transitory Emotion). 'By whom you were seen' — the similarity intended is between the strike of weapons and the eyes, the flow of blood and the flame of fire, the felling of the enemy and the burning of <s>Kāla</s> (Time/Death), and between the hero and the enemy of <s>Smara</s> (the God of Love, i.e., <s>Śiva</s>). Here, this experience of a similar other object indicated by 'by whom you were seen' — that is not the figure of <s>Smaraṇa</s> through the production of remembrance of <s>Smara</s>'s enemy [<s>Śiva</s>]; rather, it is the figure of <s>Viśeṣa</s> (Distinction), having the nature of producing another meaning [in the form of] the extinguishing of curiosity at being unable to see the enemy of <s>Smara</s>. Through seeing this, that too is established — such is the understanding. But, [one may object:] the production of an impossible other object is the definition of the figure of <s>Viśeṣa</s>; here, however, we do not observe any 'production' — to this he says: 'Of production,' and so on.

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text:
yeṣāṃ kartāraḥ udāsatete 'styarthāḥ /
yeṣāṃ vikurvate te bhavatyarthāḥ /
yeṣāṃ tu prayuñjate te karotyarthāḥ /
atodṛśiḥ prayuñjānakartṛkatvāt karotyartha eveti siddham /
nanu smararipudarśanakautukāstamaye prakṛtanāyakadarśanaṃ heturiti kāvyaliṅgaṃ kiṃ na syādityata āha-matāntara ityādi /

children.text: asmaddarśane viśeṣālaṅkāraḥ, matāntare kāvyaliṅgaṃ, smaraṇaṃ tu sarvatra na bhavatīti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: In our view, it is the figure of <s>Viśeṣa</s> (Distinction); in another view, it is <s>Kāvyaliṅga</s> (Poetic Reason); but <s>Smaraṇa</s> (Remembrance) does not apply in either case — this is the purport.
In the absence of [it being] <s>Kāvyaliṅga</s>, [the figure consists in] the impossible production [of another object], which is the cause of a special aesthetic charm (<s>Vicchitti</s>).
[Definition:] <s>Smṛti</s> (Remembrance) is where, from [the experience of] a similar [object], another similar [object] is remembered.
From dissimilarity and from being inexpressible [through the above definition], <s>Preyas</s> (the Dear) is distinguished [from <s>Smaraṇa</s>].

body.translated_text: Those whose agents are indifferent have the meaning of 'to be' (<s>astyartha</s>). Those whose agents undergo transformation have the meaning of 'to become' (<s>bhavatyartha</s>). Those whose agents employ [actively] have the meaning of 'to make' (<s>karotyartha</s>). Therefore, since 'seeing' (<s>dṛś</s>) has an agent who employs [actively], it has the meaning of 'to make' — this is established. But [one may object:] would not the seeing of the hero, which is the cause of the extinguishing of curiosity about seeing the enemy of <s>Smara</s>, constitute the figure of <s>Kāvyaliṅga</s> (Poetic Reason)? — to this he says: 'According to another view,' and so on.

body.text:
itthaṃ bhedābhedatulyatve 'laṅkārānvivicya abhedaprādhānyamadhicikīrṣurāha-tadete sādṛśyetyādi /
tatrāpyāropamūlalaṅkārāṇāṃ bījabhūtaṃ rūpakamādau sūtrayati-
body.translated_text: Having thus analyzed the figures [showing] the equal balance of difference and non-difference based on similarity, and wishing to treat primarily [those based on] non-difference, he says: 'These, [based on] similarity,' and so on. Among those, he first formulates the definition of <s>Rūpaka</s> (Metaphor), which is the seed of figures rooted in superimposition (<s>Āropa</s>):

body.text: abhedaprādhānya āropa āropaviṣayānapahnave rūpakam || 15 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Rūpaka</s> (Metaphor) is a superimposition (<s>Āropa</s>) in which non-difference is predominant and the object of superimposition is not denied. // <s>RuAss</s>_15 //

children.translated_text: But the alteration of number is justified by the individual superimposition upon each object.
He illustrates this to make it intuitively clear — 'as in some cases...' etc.
Because of the individual superimposition upon each forest fire.
Even in the hermitage of the sage <s>Kapila</s>, the number of 'many' will be justified — this is the purport.

body.translated_text:
In 'the face itself is the moon' and the like, the similarity is predominantly non-difference.
The object upon which the superimposition of moon-hood etc. is made — namely the face etc. — and the non-concealment of that object, constitutes the figure of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) — this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>.
He explains this: 'of non-difference...' etc.
The real existence of difference — this shows the distinction from <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole).
Now, explaining the meaning of the word '<s>āropa</s>' (superimposition), he analyzes the subject matter with a preliminary discussion of the objects to be excluded — 'superimposition is one thing upon another.'
For in the face etc., the apprehension (<s>adhyavasāna</s>) of something else — the moon etc. — is superimposition.
And since this is two-fold in its basis, it is grasped both by the subject (<s>viṣayin</s>) and the object (<s>viṣaya</s>).
Thus two terms are established.
When it is 'the moon only, not the face' — i.e., when there is concealment of the object — then it is the figure of <s>Apahnuti</s> (denial/concealment).
But when there is no concealment, it is <s>rūpaka</s> — this is the distinction.
He explains the technical term: 'because the subject makes the object endowed with form...'
The subject makes the object endowed with its own form — therefore it is called <s>rūpaka</s> (that which bestows form) — this is the meaning.
He reminds of the overarching topic of similarity, beginning from <s>upamā</s> — 'similarity, however...' etc.
For agreement on the subject matter, he says: '<s>upamā</s> itself...' etc.
Difference has become obscured, not concealed.
He establishes the logical priority of exposition of this superimposition-based figure over <s>utprekṣā</s> and other figures based on <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination) — 'from superimposition, through non-difference...' etc.
It is advanced — meaning: because it produces the cognition of extreme similarity, it becomes the most proximate aid to <s>rasa</s>.
The word '<s>iti</s>' gives the reason.
Because the <s>adhyavasāya</s> is thus advanced through non-difference, therefore the classification of figures based on it will be done later — this is to be supplied.
Here the following should be noted:
Of the entire group of figures to be analyzed and already analyzed here, all of them have either proximate or remote serviceability to <s>rasa</s>.
Although the proximate ones have primacy, still, because they are subtler, instruction proceeds by placing the grosser figures first.
He states the varieties: 'this, moreover, is without parts (<s>niravayava</s>)...' etc.
'<s>Paramparita</s>' means 'transmitted in succession.'
The word 'first' is a prelude to the elaboration of further varieties.
He shows the twofold nature of the partless type: 'the first...' etc.
'<s>Kevala</s>' means without the accompaniment of another <s>rūpaka</s>; '<s>mālārūpaka</s>' is one existing in the company of multiple <s>rūpakas</s>.
He states the twofold nature of the type with parts (<s>sāvayava</s>): 'the second, <s>samasta</s>...' etc.
The word '<s>vastu</s>' here means 'entity' or 'referent.'
'<s>Samastavastuviṣaya</s>' means that whose domain includes all entities without remainder, consisting of qualifier and qualified.
But where the metaphor is applied in one qualifier-portion but not in another, and in the qualified — since it operates in only a part — it is <s>ekadeśavivartin</s> (partial).
He says the <s>paramparita</s> (successive) is fourfold: 'the third, <s>śliṣṭa-aśliṣṭa</s>...' etc.
Having divided into two forms — <s>śliṣṭaśabda</s> (punning word) and <s>aśliṣṭaśabda</s> (non-punning word) — each is further divided into <s>kevala</s> (simple) and <s>mālā</s> (garland) — 'first' means this.
He concludes the discussion of varieties: 'thus, eight...' etc.
<s>Kevala-niravayava</s> (simple partless), <s>mālā-niravayava</s> (garland partless), <s>samastavastuviṣaya-sāvayava</s> (whole-object with-parts), <s>ekadeśavivarti-sāvayava</s> (partial with-parts), <s>śliṣṭaśabda-kevala-paramparita</s> (punning-simple-successive), <s>śliṣṭaśabda-mālā-paramparita</s> (punning-garland-successive), <s>aśliṣṭaśabda-kevala-paramparita</s> (non-punning-simple-successive), and <s>aśliṣṭaśabda-mālā-paramparita</s> (non-punning-garland-successive).
When the metaphor of the qualified is understood implicitly through the force of the metaphorization of the qualifier, then it is <s>samāsokti-rūpaka</s> (metaphor expressed through compounding).
Or else, it is stated through compounding.
Such and other varieties are not elaborated in detail due to their grossness — he says 'others, however...' etc.
'<s>Dāsa</s>' — the particle '<s>asmi</s>' (I am) is in the sense of the first person.
Here, the metaphorization of goosebumps as thorns is partless;
and because there is no accompaniment of another <s>rūpaka</s>, it is simple (<s>kevala</s>).
'A stream of nectar' — <s>dātra</s> means sickle; <s>lūni</s> is cutting.
Despondency at night due to separation, the arising of both — this is garland-partless.
'Endowed with breadth' — a <s>patrapātra</s> is a vessel made of <s>palāśa</s> leaves; <s>bhānitārāḥ</s> means stars.
<s>Bhakta</s> is cooked food; <s>dhana</s> means wealth; <s>śṛta</s> means cooked.
Here, because the speech of village folk encompasses all referents, it is <s>samastavastuviṣaya-sāvayava rūpaka</s> (whole-object with-parts metaphor).
'Shines' — <s>kṣitibhṛt</s> means both 'king' and 'mountain.'
<s>Nistriṃśa</s> means 'sword'; it is also the line of <s>tamāla</s> groves.
Here, the metaphorization of fame as forcibly-abducted women is understood implicitly — therefore it is <s>ekadeśavivarti-sāvayava</s> (partial with-parts).
In the '<s>kṣitibhṛt</s>' portion there is a mixture (<s>saṅkara</s>) — with this in mind he says: 'in <s>kṣitibhṛt</s>...' etc.
'What of the lotus?' etc. — Here, in 'does it not kill' etc., the prohibition of killing etc. is not intended first; the interrogative '<s>kim</s>' (what) rhetorically negates it.
Therefore the meaning 'it does kill indeed' etc. is established.
Here, the metaphorization 'the face is the moon' is the cause for the nectar attributed to the moon; with the nectar of the lips it is punning (<s>śliṣṭa</s>).
Otherwise, the introduction 'even this exists here' would not be coherent.
Therefore, being manifested through the metaphorization of the moon, it is successive (<s>paramparita</s>) and simple (<s>kevala</s>).
To show this he says: 'here, through the metaphorization of the face as the moon...' etc.
'A swan in the lake of scholars' minds' — the mind of scholars is itself the <s>Mānasa</s> lake; in it, a swan. The contraction of the <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) of enemies is the contraction of lotuses.
There, '<s>dīt</s>' means 'shines' — the garlanded-with-rays one.
The searching of fortresses — places surrounded by rivers and mountains — the very absence of that is the searching for <s>Durgā</s> (<s>Kātyāyanī</s>); there, the blue-and-red one (<s>Nīlalohita</s> = <s>Śiva</s>).
Battles are the same as fire-sticks (<s>samidh</s>); in their acceptance, <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (<s>Agni</s>).
In truth, joy itself.
In the true <s>Dākṣāyiṇī</s> (<s>Satī</s>).
Displeasure at the arrangement — <s>Dakṣa</s> is <s>Dakṣa Prajāpati</s>. In victory, priority — that same priority in relation to <s>Arjuna</s> is the prior birth; regarding <s>Bhīma</s>, a hundred years — the accusative is used in the sense of proximity.
'Deeds of the <s>Kurus</s>' — Here, regarding the metaphor of scholars' minds as the lake, when the question arises 'how can this have swan-hood?', one comprehends the pun in the word '<s>mānasa</s>.'
Through the pun thus comprehended, the swan-hood is established — therefore it is <s>śliṣṭaśabda-paramparita</s> (punning-successive).
And it is in garland form.
With this in mind he says: 'here, you yourself...' etc.
The mere semblance of the two meanings — competence and fearlessness — does not constitute a contradiction.
Alternatively, let there be a pun in that portion;
for the words <s>Dakṣa</s> and <s>Bhīma</s>, the pun is the resting place of comprehension; the other portion is illustrated here — thus everything is clear.
'I go' — <s>taraṇḍa</s> means a raft.
Here, the metaphorization as a raft is established;
the metaphorization of birth, old age, and death as an ocean depends upon it — therefore it is <s>aśliṣṭaśabda</s> (non-punning), simple (<s>kevala</s>), and successive (<s>paramparita</s>).
'A couch' — <s>paryaṅka</s> means a couch or seat.
<s>Vaṃśa</s> means both 'lineage' and 'bamboo.'
<s>Styāna</s> means 'thick' or 'dense.'
<s>Mura</s> is a particular region.
<s>Sauvidallaḥ</s> means an upper garment.
This is clearly <s>aśliṣṭaśabda-mālā-paramparita</s> (non-punning garland successive).
Now, in '<s>kṣmā-sauvidallaḥ</s>' the metaphorization of the earth as chief queen etc. is not verbal — he addresses this: 'here <s>kṣmā</s>...' etc.
What is the purpose of illustrating with examples of uneven portions? — he answers: 'such and others too...' etc.
Nevertheless, here the <s>samāsokti</s> variety and others are indicated without separate examples.
In '<s>ābhāti-kṣitibhṛt</s>' there is mixture (<s>saṅkara</s>).
In '<s>kṣmā-sauvidallaḥ</s>' the successive type is also partially variant — such are the varieties being indicated.
Not only does this successive <s>rūpaka</s> operate through positive correlation (<s>anvaya</s>); it is also possible through negative correlation (<s>vyatireka</s>) — he says 'and this...' etc.
'Of good nature' — because water in the form of good nature is utterly impossible in a desert.
Because the sky-wall is not a proper support for the activity of beautiful painting — this should be understood.
'Of evil intention' — of evil purpose, or of wicked desire.
Now, in <s>rūpaka</s>, since that which is superimposed has the status of the qualified (<s>dharmin</s>), having the gender and number of the subject is appropriate.
Regarding gender-absorption, there is a way to explain it; but sometimes number-absorption is violated.
What is the solution? — He addresses this: 'here, of the thing being superimposed...' etc.
True, gender-and-number absorption of the qualified is appropriate; regarding gender-alteration there is some solution;

nipavakāśatvādvalī śleśaḥsarvālaṅkārabādha iti siddhāntayiṣyate /
tena śleṣeṇarūpakabādha iti sodāharaṇamāha-bhramimaratimityādi /
bhramiḥ śiroghūrṇi raratiranavasthā /
ālasyam abhīṣṭatānivṛttiḥ /
pralaya indriyoparatiḥ , mūrcchrā teṣāmāndhyaṃ tamo 'ntardhūmāyamānatā, śaraurasādaḥ aṅgānāmaprabhaviṣṇutā, maraṇaṃ pratītam /
tairetaiḥ nimittairaṣṭabhiḥ viṣakāryaireva garalarūpor'thaṃ udbhāvyata iti neha viṣaśabdaśleṣo rūpakahetukaḥ /
yathā vidvanmānasa ityādau /
kintu śleṣe pūrvasiddhe rūpakahetuḥ iti /

children.text: evaṃvidhe viṣaye śleṣa eva na tu rūpakamityāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: In such a case, it is <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) only, not <s>rūpaka</s> — so say
those versed in logical reasoning — this is to be supplied.
That similarity which is predominantly characterized by non-difference is considered to be of two kinds:
through superimposition (<s>āropa</s>) and through determination (<s>adhyavasāna</s>). In the case of superimposition, it becomes <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor).

body.translated_text:
Since <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) has the capacity to be all-pervading, it will be established as a principle that <s>śleṣa</s> overrides all figures.
Therefore, that <s>śleṣa</s> overrides <s>rūpaka</s> — he states with an example: '<s>bhrami-marati</s>...' etc.
<s>Bhrami</s> is vertigo (head-spinning); <s>arati</s> is restlessness.
<s>Ālasya</s> is the cessation of desired activity.
<s>Pralaya</s> is the cessation of the senses; <s>mūrcchā</s> is their blindness; <s>tamas</s> is the state of being enveloped in inner darkness; <s>śaraurasāda</s> is the incapacity of the limbs; <s>maraṇa</s> (death) is well-known.
Through these very eight effects of poison as causes, the meaning of 'poison-form' is evoked — so here the pun on the word '<s>viṣa</s>' (poison) is not the cause of the <s>rūpaka</s>,
as in 'swan of the lake of scholars' minds' and the like.
Rather, when the pun is already established, it becomes the cause of the <s>rūpaka</s>.

children.translated_text: Because of the real existence of difference, it would not literally be <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole);
and because there is no concealment of the object, this would not be <s>apahnuti</s> (denial) either.

body.text: tato viṣayirūpeṇa rūpavān viṣaye mataḥ //
body.translated_text: Therefore, the subject is considered to make the object endowed with form by its own appearance,

body.text: āropaṇena kriyate tenaitadrūpakaṃ matam //
body.translated_text: through superimposition — therefore this is regarded as <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor).

children.translated_text: The third variety of <s>rūpaka</s> is called <s>paramparita</s> (successive).
Its establishment is seen both through similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) and through dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>).
That in which the subject is superimposed upon each of the objects individually —
the number of objects may apply, even when there is a difference in the number of the qualified entities.
If the <s>rūpaka</s> that is already established gives rise to <s>śleṣa</s> (pun),
then it remains <s>rūpaka</s>; otherwise, it is considered <s>śleṣa</s>.

body.text: atha rūpakātprakṛtopayogalakṣaṇavaidharmyaśāline pariṇāmālaṅkārāya sūtram-
body.translated_text: Now, for the figure of <s>Pariṇāma</s> (transformation), which differs from <s>rūpaka</s> by the characteristic of serviceability to the contextual meaning — the <s>sūtra</s> states:

body.text: āropyamāṇāsya prakṛtopayogitve pariṇāmaḥ || 16 ||
body.translated_text: When the superimposed element serves the contextual meaning (<s>prakṛtopayogitva</s>), it is <s>Pariṇāma</s> (transformation). || <s>RuAss</s> 16 ||

body.text:
prakṛtopayogitvaṃ vivicya darśayitumāha-āropyamāṇaṃ rūpakam ityādi /
āropyamāṇaṃ candratvādi /
prakṛtopayogitvābhāvāditi /
prakṛtaṃ mukhādi, tatropayogitvaṃ vākyārthānupraveśaparyantamāropaṇavivakṣāyāṃ syāt /
tadvi rūpake nsti /
"mukhameva candra'ityetāvataiva rūpakatvasiddhiḥ /
tasmādāropyamāṇaṃ candratvādimukhādau prakṛtārthe tādrūpyapratītyādhānarūpeṇa uparañjakatvenaiva rūpakālaṅkāre 'nvayaṃ bhajate /
pariṇāmetviti /
pariṇāmālaṅkāre punaḥ āropyamāṇaṃ na kevalaṃ prakṛtoparañjakaṃ yāvatā prakṛtarūpamapahnuvānaṃ sattadātmatvenopayujyate /
ata iha vākyānupraveśāntam āropavivakṣā /
sā cāprakṛtasya prakṛtarūpāpattāvevopayujyate /
na punaḥ rūpakavat prakṛtasya aprakṛtarūpāpattau /
tadetadāha-prakṛtamāropyamāṇa rūpatvenetyādi /
atraitadupahvaram /
āropasya dviṣṭhatve 'pi prakṛtāprakṛtayornaikavidhā vṛttiḥ /
viṣaya viṣayitvena vivakṣā niyamāt /
viṣayaḥ khalu ādheyaguṇa eva bhavati /
viṣayī punarguṇādhāttaiva bhavati /
itthaṃ ca sati viṣayitvāropaṇaṃ viṣaye tādrūpyapratītimātraṃ cedvivakṣyate, tadā tādrūpyapratīti janakatva mātramu parañjakatvam itye tāvataiva āropaṇasya caritārthatā /
atastādrūpyapratītimātra prasiddhyarthaṃ prakṛtam (a)prakṛta rūpāpānnaṃ bhavati rūpake /
pariṇāme tu prakṛtopayogāntamāropavivakṣayeti /
svarūpādapracyutasyaiva prakṛtasyāprakṛtarūpo pagrāhitvalakṣaṇāvasthāntarāpattireva /

children.text: itarathā rūpakanyāyena prakṛtasya svarūpasthaganena prakṛtameva na pratīyeta /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, by the logic of <s>rūpaka</s>, through the concealment of the contextual element's own nature, the contextual element itself would not be cognized.

children.text: kā tatra prakṛtopayogitā? tadabhāve ca kā rūpakasya viviktaviṣayatā? prāyeṇātra prācāmācāryāṇām api vyāmohakalānuvṛttiriti rahasyamuddhāṭitam /
children.translated_text: What serviceability to the contextual meaning would there be then? And in its absence, what distinct domain would <s>rūpaka</s> have? In this matter, even the earlier teachers have generally followed the ways of confusion — this secret has now been revealed.

For a summary of the analysis distinguishing the domains of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) and <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation), here are two subsidiary verses: 'When, by superimposing the form of the standard upon the subject, the subject is concealed —'
'Then it is <s>rūpaka</s>-ness; there the connection is through embellishment.'

body.translated_text:
He analyzes and shows what serviceability to the contextual meaning is — 'the superimposed element, which is <s>rūpaka</s>...' etc.
The superimposed element is moon-hood etc.
'Because of the absence of serviceability to the contextual meaning' — the contextual meaning is the face etc.; serviceability to it would occur when the superimposition is intended to extend into the meaning of the entire sentence.
That does not exist in <s>rūpaka</s>.
In 'the face itself is the moon' — by this much alone the status of <s>rūpaka</s> is established.
Therefore, the superimposed element — moon-hood etc. — participates in the figure of <s>rūpaka</s> only in the capacity of embellishing the contextual meaning (face etc.) by serving as a basis for the cognition of similarity.
In <s>Pariṇāma</s>, however — in the figure of transformation — the superimposed element is not merely an embellisher of the contextual meaning; rather, concealing the contextual form, it is employed as having that very nature.
Therefore, here the intention of superimposition extends to the entry into the sentence's meaning.
And that is employed only when the non-contextual element assumes the form of the contextual —
not, as in <s>rūpaka</s>, when the contextual assumes the form of the non-contextual.
This he states: 'the contextual element, through the form of the superimposed...' etc.
Here the following should be noted:
Even though superimposition is two-sided, the function of the contextual and non-contextual is not of one kind.
Because the intention is determined as subject and object.
The object indeed becomes the recipient of qualities;
the subject becomes the bestower of qualities.
Thus, if the superimposition of the subject onto the object is intended to produce merely the cognition of similarity, then the mere production of that cognition of similarity constitutes the embellishment — and by that much the purpose of the superimposition is fulfilled.
Therefore, for the mere establishment of the cognition of similarity, the contextual element takes on the non-contextual form — this is <s>rūpaka</s>.
In <s>Pariṇāma</s>, however, the intention of superimposition extends to serviceability to the contextual meaning.
Of the contextual element, while not departing from its own nature, the assumption of a different state characterized by the adoption of the non-contextual form —

children.translated_text: 'But when the subject, without departing from its own form,'
'Assumes another's form for the purpose of utility, that is considered <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation).'

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text:

tathāhi-dharmapariṇāmo lakṣaṇapariṇāmo 'vasthāpariṇāmaśceti tridhā pariṇāmaḥ saṅkhyātaḥ /
tatra lakṣaṇapariṇāmatkimasya vaidharmyamityata āha-āgamānugametyādi /
āptoktirāgamaḥ /
anugamo vyātpiḥ /
vyāvṛttirvigamaḥ /

children.translated_text: Due to the absence of that [conformity with tradition], there is a distinction between the two.

children.text: na khalvayaṃ kāvye lakṣaṇapariṇāmaḥ āgamarūpeṇa vā anumānarūpeṇa vā khyā (ta i)tyalaṃ prasaṃgena bahunā /
children.translated_text: This characteristic-transformation in poetry is certainly not known in the form of tradition (<s>āgama</s>) or in the form of inference (<s>anumāna</s>) — enough with this lengthy digression.

children.text: tatrāpi sāṅkhyayogādiśāstraviṣayeṇa pratijñātaṃ khalvasmābhiḥ śrīguruprasādasamanantaraṃ śaiśava eva yathā - "śaivaṃ viṣṇunibaddhamaupaniṣadaṃ sāṅkhyaṃ sapātañjalaṃ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, regarding <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, and other philosophical systems, we have indeed made a declaration, by the grace of our illustrious teacher, in youth itself, as follows: '<s>Śaiva</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, <s>Aupaniṣadika</s>, <s>Sāṅkhya</s> together with <s>Pātañjala</s> [Yoga],'
'The <s>Śāstras</s> (treatises) for the benefit of one's own self, the <s>Vedas</s> with all the <s>Purāṇas</s> and other [texts],'

body.translated_text:
Now, this characteristic-transformation (<s>lakṣaṇa-pariṇāma</s>) has also been described by the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> [philosophers].
Thus: transformation is threefold in <s>Sāṅkhya</s> reckoning — transformation of property (<s>dharma-pariṇāma</s>), transformation of characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa-pariṇāma</s>), and transformation of condition (<s>avasthā-pariṇāma</s>).
How does this differ from the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> characteristic-transformation? To answer this he says: 'by conformity with tradition (<s>āgama</s>),' etc.
<s>Āgama</s> (tradition) is the statement of an authority (<s>āpta</s>).
<s>Anugama</s> (conformity) is comprehension.
<s>Vigama</s> (departure) is exclusion.

children.text: bhūtānāṃ tu vinodanāya bharataṃ nīrti ca vātsyāyanaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'And for the entertainment of beings: the <s>Bharata</s> [<s>Nāṭyaśāstra</s>], <s>Nīti</s> (political science), and <s>Vātsyāyana</s> [<s>Kāmasūtra</s>],'
'And poetry with its theory in six languages — [all this is mastered by] <s>Śrī Cakravartin</s> the poet.'

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: spardhayā sisādhayiṣu (ṣūn)dustārkikajaradgavān pratyāpahālaparasya mamāyamanyaḥ ślokaḥ- sāṅkhyaṃ veśmani veśmani śrutiśiraḥ kakṣyāsu kakṣyāsu ca dvāri dvāri śivāgamāḥ pathi pathi prācāṃ kavīnāṃ giraḥ /
children.translated_text: Another verse of mine, eager to defeat — out of rivalry — the decrepit old logicians who attempt refutation: 'In every household <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, in every courtyard the crests of the <s>Śruti</s> (Upaniṣads), at every door the <s>Śaiva Āgamas</s>, on every path the words of the ancient poets —'
'That all this is recited by envious, dull-witted, senile logicians — that itself is the drum of the fame of the learning of <s>Cakravartin</s> the poet!'

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text:
mahārāja vīraballālāsthānajuṣāṃ viduṣāṃ prasādāśiṣo hi mayyetāḥ prathante /
kāstāḥ? saṃskṛtasārvabhaumaḥ , prākṛta pṛthvīśvaraḥ śaurasenī śiromaṇi magidhīmakaradhvajaḥ ṣaiśācīparameśvaro 'pabhraṃśarājahaṃso 'laṅkāracakravartī dhvaniprasthānaparamācāryaḥ sahajasarvajña(ḥ)paramayogīśvaraḥ śaivavaiṣṇavayogasāṅkhyapramukhasamastasvātmavidyātattvaniṣṇā(taḥ)śrutādhigatasamastavidyākalāpo 'dvaitavidyāvidveṣivanadāvānala(ḥ) kaliyugaskanda(ḥ)abhinavabhaṭṭācaryavaidikavidyāpratiṣṭhāpanaparamācārya(ḥ)kāvyamīmāṃsāprābhākaravādimṛgendra(ḥ) veśaṣyābhujaṅga ityādyā mahārājahosalarāja kuladvāri praśasti śilāśāsanaprabhṛtibhiḥ vayamupaśāntarabhasāḥ /
atra tu granthe kāvyamīmāṃ(sā)nikaṣatāṃ mamopayāntu vatsalāḥsacetasaḥ /
prakṛtamanusarāmaḥ /
sā cāyaṃ pariṇāmālaṅkāro dvirūpa iti vyutpādayati-tasya sāmānādhikaraṇyetyādi /
tīrtveti /
dhunī sarit /
ātmanā tṛtīya ityanena sītāsaumitrivyatiriktaparijanavisarjanaṃ pratyāyyate /
ātarastaraṇapaṇyam /
tasmai nāvikāya guhāya /
vyāmaśabdena tatparimāṇāmucyate tadiha bāhudvayaṃ lakṣayati /
tadgrāhyastanītvena tu kṛcchrānuyāne heturūpanyastaḥ /
atrātarasyā prakṛtasyā na kevalaṃ maitrītādrūpyapratītimātraṃ vivakṣyate, api tu nadītaraṇapratyupakaraṇātmakaṃ prakṛtopayogitvamapi /
ataḥ aprakṛtasya prakṛtarūpāpannasya prakṛtopayoga iti prakṛtasya svarūpādapracyuteḥ pariṇāmatvam /
tadetaddarśayitumāha-atra saumitrimaitrītyādi /
samānādhikaraṇagrahaṇaṃ prathamaprakāratvaprathanāya /
prakṛtarūpāpannasya prakṛtopayoga iti pariṇāmabījabhūtaṃ upayogitvamuddhāṭayitumāha-bhrātasasya maitrītyādi /

children.text: yata itthaṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyaprayoge pariṇāmālaṅkārasya viṣayavyavasthātasmāt samāsoktisādharmyamastīti vyutpipādayuṣurupakramate-tavatra yathetyādinā /
children.translated_text: Since in the co-referential usage there is the domain of the <s>pariṇāma</s> figure, and therefore there is a resemblance with <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) — wishing to explain [the distinction], he begins with: 'here, as...' etc.
<s>Samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) will be stated [as]: when, through the similarity of qualifying properties, the non-contextual is understood.

children.text: upoḍharāgeṇa vilolatārakaṃ tathā gṛhītaṃ śaśinā nasāmukham /
children.translated_text: 'Her face, seized by the moon with aroused passion and trembling pupils,'

children.text: yathā samastaṃ timirāṃśukaṃ tayā puro 'pi rāgādgalitaṃ na lakṣitam //
children.translated_text: 'Was [held] in such a way that the entire veil of darkness slipped away before her, unnoticed, due to passion.'

body.translated_text:
The blessings and favors of the scholars who attended the court of the great king <s>Vīra Ballāla</s> have indeed spread upon me.
What are those [titles]? Emperor of Sanskrit, Lord of <s>Prākrit</s>, Crest-jewel of <s>Śaurasenī</s>, Crocodile-banner of <s>Māgadhī</s>, Supreme Lord of <s>Paiśācī</s>, Royal Swan of <s>Apabhraṃśa</s>, Emperor of Ornaments, Supreme Teacher of the <s>Dhvani</s> school, Naturally Omniscient, Supreme Lord of Yogins, Expert in the truth of all self-knowledge systems led by <s>Śaiva</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, and <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, Possessor of all arts and sciences learned and studied, Forest-fire to the enemies of <s>Advaita</s> (non-dual) knowledge, <s>Skanda</s> of the <s>Kali</s> age, Supreme teacher for establishing the Vedic learning of the new <s>Bhaṭṭācārya</s>, Lion among debaters of <s>Kāvya-mīmāṃsā</s> (literary criticism) and <s>Prābhākara</s> [Mīmāṃsā], Serpent to <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> [philosophy], and so on — with such titles on stone-inscription eulogies at the gateway of the royal <s>Hoysaḷa</s> dynasty, we have become tranquil in our fervor.
But in this treatise, let the affectionate and discerning [readers] approach me as a touchstone of literary criticism.
Let us follow the topic at hand.
He [the author] explains that this figure of <s>pariṇāma</s> is of two kinds: '<s>tasya sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>' etc.
'Having crossed' (<s>tīrtvā</s>): <s>dhunī</s> means river.
'By himself' — the instrumental 'by himself' conveys the dismissal of attendants other than <s>Sītā</s> and <s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>).
<s>Ātara</s> is the fare for crossing.
For that ferryman <s>Guha</s>.
By the word <s>vyāma</s> (fathom), its measure is expressed; here it denotes the two arms.
The grasping of those [arms] in their breast-nature presents a reason in the form of the difficulty of following.
Here, it is not merely the perception of the similarity of the <s>ātara</s> (fare) with friendship, but also the utility to the contextual subject — namely, the reciprocal assistance in crossing the river.
Therefore, since the non-contextual thing assumes the form of the contextual and serves the contextual purpose, and since the contextual thing does not depart from its own nature, it is <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation).
To demonstrate this, he says: 'Here, the friendship of <s>Saumitri</s>...' etc.
The use of 'co-referential' (<s>samānādhikaraṇa</s>) is to indicate that this is the first type.
To reveal the utility — which is the seed of <s>pariṇāma</s> — namely that the non-contextual, having assumed the form of the contextual, serves the contextual, he says: 'the friendship of the brother...' etc.

body.text:
atropoḍarāgatvavilolatārakatvādihetunā nāyikānāyakayoḥ dharmaviśeṣaḥ gṛhītaḥ /
na lakṣita[mi]ti vākyānupreśāntaṃ vivakṣita iti prakṛtopayogī /
sa cāropaviṣayabhūtasandhyārāganakṣatrādirūpeṇaivāste /
anena prakṛtasya svarūpādapracyutirdarśitā /
ato vyavahārāntamāropaḥ /
na tu rūpakanyāyena rūpasamāropamātramityaṃśe pariṇāmasamāsoktyoḥ sādharmyamavagantavyamityata āha-evamihāpīti /
tarhi kimanayormitho vailakṣaṇyamityāha-kevalaṃ tatretyādi /
prayogaḥ śabdenopādānam /
nanu yadi dvayoḥ prayogastarhi pariṇāmatvameva kathamityata āha-tādātmyāttviti /
na khalu tādātmye sati "kṣīraṃ dadhīti" prayogamātrāt pariṇāmatvahāniḥ /
vaidharmyeṇodāharati-atha paktrimatāmiti /
pāko [viklittiḥ] /
paktrimatā prayojanavat lakṣaṇaprācuryam /
vakraḥ panthāḥ /
tadiśritaistadavalambibhiḥ /
tatparataḥ tadanantaram /

children.translated_text: Here, for connecting the characteristics, he says: 'here, the arrangement of kings...' etc.
By the word 'appropriate,' the contextual nature is indicated.
'When that which is being superimposed upon the contextual subject is utilized [for the contextual purpose],'
'That is <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation); by this it is distinguished from <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor).'

body.translated_text:
Here, the specific quality of the heroine and hero is apprehended through the reasoning of aroused-passion, trembling-pupils, etc.
'Was not noticed' — [the narrative] enters the sentence-conclusion as the intended meaning and thus serves the contextual purpose.
And it remains in the form of the twilight-glow, stars, etc. that are the objects of superimposition.
By this, the non-departure of the contextual from its own nature is shown.
Hence the superimposition extends to [actual] behavior.
But the resemblance of <s>pariṇāma</s> and <s>samāsokti</s> should not be understood as mere superimposition of form in the manner of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) — hence he says: 'thus here too...' etc.
Then what is the mutual distinction between the two? He says: 'only there...' etc.
'Usage' (<s>prayoga</s>) means verbal employment.
But if both are employed, then how can it be <s>pariṇāma</s>? He answers: 'because of identity...' etc.
For when there is identity, the <s>pariṇāma</s>-ness is not lost merely from the usage 'milk is curds.'
He illustrates with a contrast: 'now, maturity of cooking...' etc.
'Cooking' is transformation [through heat].
'Maturity of cooking' means abundance of the characteristic that has a purpose.
'Crooked path' — a winding road.
'Dependent on that' means reliant on that.
'After that' means following that.

children.translated_text: 'In <s>rūpaka</s>, the [non-contextual] embellishes through mere superimposition of form;'
'Here [in <s>pariṇāma</s>], there is connection with the contextual through superimposition of behavior.'
'The distinction between <s>pariṇāma</s> and <s>samāsokti</s> should be understood from this reversal:'
'The difference between the two consists in the employment or non-employment [of both terms].'

body.text: viṣayasya sandihyamānatve sandehaḥ || 17 ||
body.translated_text: When the identity of the subject is in doubt, that is <s>sandeha</s> (doubt). || <s>RuAss</s> 17 ||

body.text:
saṅgatyarthamadhikāram anusmārayati-"abhedaprādhānya ityādi" /
nanu viṣayatve nirjñāte 'kaḥsandeha ityāha-viṣaya(ḥ) prakṛta ityādi' /
nirjñātameva ṇukhādilakṣaṇaṃ prakṛtamarthaṃ bhittī kṛtya candrādāvaprakṛter'thesandihyamāne sandehasya dviṣṭhatvāt prakṛtor'tho 'pi sandehaḍolāmadhirohati /
itthaṃ prakṛtāprakṛtagatatvena ya utthāpyate pratibhayaiva sandehaḥ, sa sandeho 'laṅkāraḥ na tu sthāṇupuruṣādāviva svarasavāhī /
tadviśeṣārthamāha-sa ca trividha ityādi /
kiṃ tāruṇyeti /
utkalikā utkaṇṭhā samayaḥ sampradāyaḥ upadeśayaṣṭirakṣaranirdeśadaṇḍaḥ /

children.translated_text: '<s>Śṛṅgārin</s>' — the goddess is <s>Manmatha</s> (Kāma, the god of love).
Here, because no resolution is adopted, the doubt is pure.
He analyzes and shows the resolution-containing [type]: '<s>niścaya</s>' (resolution) etc.
Since the telling comes at the end of the doubt, the resolution or semblance of resolution in the middle should be traced.

body.translated_text:
To recall the governing topic for the purpose of connection, he says: '<s>abhedaprādhānya</s>' (predominance of non-difference) etc.
But when the subject-hood is ascertained, what doubt can there be? He answers: 'the subject is the contextual...' etc.
Even when the contextual meaning characterized by the moon-face etc. has been ascertained, when there is doubt regarding the non-contextual meaning such as the [actual] moon — since the doubt has two bases, the contextual meaning too mounts the swing of doubt.
Thus the doubt that is raised by poetic imagination regarding both the contextual and non-contextual is the figure of <s>sandeha</s> (doubt) — not a spontaneous [real] doubt as in the case of the stump-or-person [scenario].
To specify this he says: 'and it is threefold...' etc.
'Is it youth?' — <s>utkalikā</s> means eager longing; <s>samaya</s> means tradition; <s>upadeśayaṣṭi</s> means the rod of instruction in the form of letter-designation.

body.text:
ayaṃ mārtaṇḍa iti /
itaḥ prātpaḥ /
sarvā diśo na prasaratīti ūrdhva jvalanaikasvabhāva rūpatvāt /
tirastiryak /
atrāsaṅkhya turagatvā dinā mārtaṇḍatvadisandehāpagama eva jāyate /
tena punarnāyakasya śṛṅgrāhikayā rūpanirjñānamiti niścayābhāsā ete /
ata eva punaḥsaṃśayot thānamiti niścayagarbhatā /
tṛtīyaṃ vivecayati-niścayāntaḥ ityādi /
induḥ kimiti /
parato niścitamiti kathanāt dvitīyārdhānte itthaṃ sandihyetyadhyāhāryam /
kvacitpunarviṣaye saṃśayitavye 'pira āropyamāṇānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ viṣayāntaratvamapi bhavatīti āha-kvacidityādi /

children.translated_text: '<s>Rañjitā</s>' (colored) — thus.
'Colored' means led to another color.
'Condensed' (<s>saṃhṛtāḥ</s>) means contracted.
Here he shows the different basis: 'here, the superimposition...' etc.

body.translated_text:
'This is the sun (<s>Mārtaṇḍa</s>)' — thus: 'from here, the dawn.'
'It does not spread in all directions' — because it has the nature of burning only upward.
'Across' means horizontally.
Here, the removal of the doubt of being the sun arises from the [observation of] countless horses and daylight.
Therefore, the recognition of the hero's <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) form does not constitute a [true] resolution — hence these are semblances of resolution.
Therefore, the renewed arising of doubt constitutes the resolution-containing nature.
He analyzes the third [type]: '<s>niścayāntaḥ</s>' (ending in resolution) etc.
'Is it the moon?' — Since the telling thereafter says 'it is resolved,' the words 'thus there would be doubt' should be supplied.
Sometimes, however, even when the subject is to be doubted, the properties being superimposed may also belong to another subject — he says: 'sometimes...' etc.

body.text: nanvatra sambhāvanāpi pratīyata iti kathaṃ sandehālaṅkāra ityata āha-kecidadhyavasāyetyādi //
body.translated_text: But here <s>sambhāvanā</s> (supposition) is also perceived — so how can this be the figure of <s>sandeha</s> (doubt)? He answers: 'some [say] <s>adhyavasāya</s>...' etc.

body.text:
adhyavasāyaḥ utprekṣaṇam /
utprekṣāśrayo 'yaṃ sandeha iti kecit /
utprekṣaivetyanye /

children.translated_text: In both cases, the reason is that the particle <s>nu</s> indicates doubt and supposition.
But in reality, there is no perception of supposition here.
Because deliberation (<s>vitarka</s>) does not incline toward any one alternative.
Therefore, this is purely a doubt swinging between alternatives — this is the purport.

body.translated_text:
<s>Adhyavasāya</s> means poetic fancy (<s>utprekṣaṇa</s>).
Some say this doubt is based on <s>utprekṣā</s> (fancy).
Others say it is <s>utprekṣā</s> itself.

children.translated_text: 'If the doubt, through the contextual subject, touches upon the non-contextual —'
'This doubt raised by poetic imagination is considered the figure of <s>sandeha</s> (doubt).'

body.text: atha bhrāntimataḥ sūtram /
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>sūtra</s> on <s>bhrāntimān</s> (delusion):

body.text: sādṛśyādvastvantarapratītirbhrāntimān || 18 ||
body.translated_text: The perception of another thing due to similarity is <s>bhrāntimān</s> (delusion). || <s>RuAss</s> 18 ||

children.translated_text: The meaning is: erroneous cognition caused by similarity is <s>bhrāntimān</s>.
For the purpose of connection, he says: 'erroneous cognition...' etc.
He explains the defined term: '<s>bhrānti</s> is [an attribute] of the mind...' etc.
Lest the mere mental attribute be an ornament — anticipating this objection, he says: 'caused by similarity...' etc.
'On the lip, a <s>bimba</s> [fruit]' — thus.

body.text:
śoṇo maṇirmāṇikyam /
niṣpatya ālīya sādṛśyāditi yaduktaṃ tatra pratyudājihīrṣurāha-gāḍhamarmetyādi /
dāmodareti /
vakṣorūpamarmacūrṇanaṃ nabhasaḥ śatacandratvena hetuḥ /
sādṛśyahetukāpi lokavilakṣaṇaiva bhrāntiralaṅkārabījamityāha-sādṛśyahetu kāpītyādi /
vicchrittiralaukikī śobhā /

children.translated_text: 'Like mother-of-pearl silver' — thus.
The meaning is: 'as in the case of silver [perceived] in mother-of-pearl.'

children.text: alaukikatvanayo 'yaṃ sandehe 'pi samāna iti vyutpādayati-evaṃ sthāṇurityādi /
children.translated_text: This principle of extraordinariness applies equally to <s>sandeha</s> (doubt) as well — he explains: 'thus, the stump...' etc.
'The delusion raised by similarity — where that occurs, it is considered <s>bhrāntimān</s> (delusion).'

body.translated_text:
'Red gem' means ruby.
'Having descended [upon it]' — having alighted [on the lip] due to similarity — to counter what was said, he says: 'deeply wounding...' etc.
'<s>Dāmodara</s>' [a name of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] — the crushing of the vital spot that is the chest serves as the reason for the sky becoming 'hundred-mooned' [i.e., full of wounds/marks].
Even delusion caused by similarity, when extraordinary to the world, is the seed of the ornament — he says: 'even caused by similarity...' etc.
<s>Vicchitti</s> means extraordinary beauty.

body.text: " athollekhālaṅkārāya sūtram-
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>sūtra</s> for the figure of <s>ullekha</s> (multiple perception) —

body.text: ekasyāpi nimittavaśādanekadhā grahaṇamullekhaḥ || 19 ||
body.translated_text: The apprehension of one and the same thing in multiple ways due to [different] causes is <s>ullekha</s> (multiple perception). || <s>RuAss</s> 19 ||

body.text:
ekasyāpi vastuno nānāvidhadharmayoga nimittavaśādanekadhāgrahe satyullekhālaṅkāraḥ /
tacca anekadhātvaṃ gṛhītṛbhedādbhavati viṣayabhedādvā bhavati /
tadetad vyācaṣṭe-yatraṅkaṃ vastvityādi /
yatroktiprakāre /
gṛhyate jñāyate /
ullekhanaṃ nurdhāraṇam /
nānāvidhadharmābhāve tvanekadhāgrahaṇamātreṇā nollekha ityāha-na cedamityādi /
etatkriyate, ullekhanaṃ niṣpādyata ityarthaḥ /
nanu nānāvidhadharmayogamātrānnonokadhāgrahaṇamanupaśyāmaḥ ityata āha-tatra ca rucyarthitvetyādi /
rucirabhiratiḥ /
arthitvaṃ lipsā /
vyatpattiḥ śabdārthamaṅketajñānam /
yathāyogamiti /
yodo yogyatā /
tāmanatikramya rucyādiṣu triṣu yathāyogamekaṃ dvayaṃ trayameva vā prayojakaṃ bhavatītiyāvat /
tatra saṃvādāyāha-taduktam /
yathārucītyādi /
rurcyarthitvavyutpattyanusāreṇa ekasminnapyanusandhānena sādhite nirdhāriter'the ābhāsaḥ pratītirbhidyate /
nānollekhātmikā jāyata ityarthaḥ /
yastapovanamityādi /
eka eva śrīkaṇṭhajanapadaḥ munyādibhistapovanatvādyākāreṇa gṛhyate /
tathā cānekadhā grahaṇe tapovanatvādinānāvidhadharmayogo nimittam /
janapade hi tapovanatvādi dharmā nisargata eva santi /
itarathā nollekhaḥ /
rūpakatvaprātpeḥ /
lakṣaṇaṃ yojayati-atrahyeka evetyādi /
samastā vyastā iti munyādīnāṃ tapovanā ditvenollekhe tathāvidhā rucyādayo hi samastatayā vyastatayā vā saṃbhavanti /
viṣayapariśuddhyai codayati-nanvetanmadhye ityādi /
vajrapañjaratvāderhi tapodityādi /
na tāvadasya rūpakaviviktaviṣayatā nāsti /

children.translated_text: '<s>Nidarśanīya</s>' means 'to be illustrated.'
In some readings, '<s>kārakāntara</s>' (another case-relation) is the reading.
If a single thing, by the force of various properties, is apprehended as though it were many,
that is called <s>ullekha</s> (delineation), because of the delineation of various forms.

body.translated_text: When a single object is apprehended in multiple ways due to its connection with various different properties, that is the figure of <s>ullekha</s> (delineation). And this multiplicity of apprehension arises either from a difference of apprehenders or from a difference of aspects. He explains this: '<s>yatra ekaṃ vastu</s>' etc. '<s>Yatra</s>' means 'in which mode of expression.' '<s>Gṛhyate</s>' means 'is known.' '<s>Ullekhana</s>' means 'ascertainment.' But when there is no connection with various properties, mere manifold apprehension does not constitute <s>ullekha</s>—he states this: '<s>na cedam</s>' etc. 'This is done, this is accomplished'—such is the meaning. Now, we do not see how manifold apprehension arises from the mere connection with various properties—to address this he says '<s>tatra ca rucy-arthitva</s>' etc. '<s>Ruci</s>' means delight. '<s>Arthitva</s>' means desire. '<s>Vyutpatti</s>' means knowledge of the connection between words and meanings. '<s>Yathāyogam</s>' means '<s>yoga</s>' is appropriateness; without transgressing it, among the three—<s>ruci</s> etc.—one, two, or all three serve as the motivating cause, as appropriate—such is the purport. For concordance with that, he says '<s>taduktam</s>,' '<s>yathāruci</s>' etc. Following <s>ruci</s>, <s>arthitva</s>, and <s>vyutpatti</s>, even when the meaning is established through a single investigation, the apprehension is differentiated—various <s>ullekha</s>-like cognitions arise—such is the meaning. '<s>Yastapovanam</s>' etc.—one and the same <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> region is apprehended by sages and others under the aspects of being a forest of austerities etc. And in this manifold apprehension, the connection with various properties like being a forest of austerities is the cause. For in the region, properties like being a forest of austerities exist naturally. Otherwise it would not be <s>ullekha</s>—because it would devolve into <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor). He applies the definition: '<s>atra hy eka eva</s>' etc. '<s>Samastā vyastā</s>'—for the sages etc., in the <s>ullekha</s> as a forest of austerities etc., such <s>ruci</s> etc. can occur either collectively or separately. To refine the scope, he raises an objection: '<s>nanu etan madhye</s>' etc. For '<s>vajrapañjaratva</s>' etc.—this is not without a domain distinct from <s>rūpaka</s>. But where the aspect is <s>rūpaka</s>, if the distinctive delight characteristic of <s>ullekha</s> does not occur, then there is no dispute. But if it does occur, then it is simply a case of overlap (<s>saṅkara</s>). Its own nature cannot be denied. To show the distinct domain of this from <s>bhrāntimān</s> (delusion), he raises an objection: '<s>evaṃ tarhi</s>' etc. '<s>Tatra</s>'—meaning 'in the domain that is distinct from <s>rūpaka</s>.' He exposes the seed of the suspicion of <s>bhrāntimān</s>: '<s>ata drūpata</s>' etc. Although properties like being a forest of austerities do exist in the region, in reality the region is not of that nature. Therefore, the apprehension of what is not of that nature as if it were of that nature is <s>bhrāntimān</s>—such is the purport. He refutes this: '<s>naitat</s>. <s>Anekedha</s>' etc. For the variety that is the form of manifold apprehension is not possessed even by <s>bhrāntimān</s> with its own defining characteristics—to address this he says '<s>saṅkarapravṛttistu</s>' etc. To distinguish its domain also from <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), he raises a doubt: '<s>yadyevam abhede bheda</s>' etc. For in reality, from the standpoint of the component parts like forest of austerities, there is no difference of the whole, namely the region. Thus, when there is no difference, the figure 'difference in non-difference,' which is <s>atiśayokti</s>, should apply here—what need for a separate concept?—such is the thrust of the objection. He refutes: '<s>na eṣa doṣaḥ</s>. <s>Grahītṛbheda</s>' etc. For in <s>atiśayokti</s>, the difference of apprehenders is not employed. But here it is employed. Therefore this is not merely <s>atiśayokti</s>. And the productive function of the difference of apprehenders should not be doubted—he says '<s>tasya ca</s>' etc. Since this is the case, its subsumption under another figure is not at all possible. He illustrates with an example that is unmixed with <s>rūpaka</s>: '<s>ṇārāaṇa</s>' etc. The aged women see him as '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'; the young women see him as 'the beloved of <s>Śrī</s>'; the girls see him with mere curiosity, just as he is. Here, when the one <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> enters the city, the aged women see him directly as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> who grants liberation—because their <s>ruci</s> etc. are of that kind. The young women see him as the life-beloved of <s>Lakṣmī</s>. And the girls see him with mere curiosity, just as he is. The particle '<s>evam eva</s>' is intended in the sense of 'whatever.' Nor should it be objected that since another motivating factor, namely curiosity, is mentioned, <s>ruci</s> etc. are not the motivating factors here—because curiosity is impossible without <s>ruci</s> and the like. Having thus illustrated from the difference of apprehenders, he illustrates from the difference of aspects: '<s>evaṃ gururvacasi</s>' etc. In speech as the aspect, he is <s>guru</s> (weighty, i.e. a teacher), being authoritative, not to be transgressed, and also <s>Vācaspati</s> (lord of speech). Then on the chest, he is <s>Pṛthu</s> (broad), being expansive, the king named <s>Pṛthu</s>. In fame, he is <s>Arjuna</s> (bright), being spotless, and also <s>Dhanañjaya</s> (winner of wealth). In these and similar cases, the one hero being described is apprehended in multiple ways through the difference of aspects, without depending on the difference of apprehenders, through the force of <s>ruci</s> etc.—hence it constitutes the figure of <s>ullekha</s>. To show the internal dissimilarity between the two modes, he says '<s>iyāṃ tu</s>' etc. He raises a doubt about the absence of <s>ullekha</s> here: '<s>nanu ayam</s>' etc. For it will be stated that <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) overrides all other figures. Therefore, when a figure with its own proper definition exists, it should not apply when <s>śleṣa</s> is present—hence <s>ullekha</s> is not appropriate here—such is the objection. He refutes: '<s>satyam</s>' etc. True, by the stated principle, <s>ullekha</s> is overridden by <s>śleṣa</s>. Nevertheless, since that which does not exist in its own form cannot be overridden, the very overriding is evidence for the existence of <s>ullekha</s>. Through the force of the distinctive delight in the form of manifold apprehension, <s>ullekha</s> shines forth—such is the purport. Since this is the case, its total absence should not be maintained—it is a distinct figure. To establish this very point, he demonstrates the independence from <s>śleṣa</s> in this same example: '<s>yad evaṃvidha</s>' etc. Here, even in the absence of <s>śleṣa</s>—'not to be transgressed in speech, expansive on the chest, spotless in fame'—there is no absence of <s>ullekha</s>. Because this is so, in such domains <s>ullekha</s> itself, being the specific source of delight compared to other figures, is superior, more praiseworthy—such is the meaning. Thus, by the principle that it can be the basis of the delight of other figures like <s>rūpaka</s>, <s>atiśayokti</s>, <s>śleṣa</s>, etc., this figure can also arise as the basis of delight of yet another figure. But that should be investigated independently. Since the principle has been demonstrated—with this intent he says '<s>evam alaṅkārāntara</s>' etc.

children.translated_text: That which is one is indeed apprehended as many, from the difference of forms.
If the multiplicity in the world arises naturally from the force of <s>ruci</s> (taste) and the like,
this is not considered to be <s>bhrānti</s> (delusion), which consists in the identification of what is not of that nature as being of that nature.
Nor can it be <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), which posits difference in non-difference.
In the first kind, there is no multiplicity of apprehension; and in the last, there is no difference of apprehenders.
Without the difference of aspects or apprehenders, <s>ullekha</s> is not possible.

children.text: yadyapi śleṣato bādho na tathāpyasya nihnavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even though there is overriding by <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), its denial is not appropriate.
For even independently of <s>śleṣa</s>, it deserves to stand just as it is.

body.text: athāpahnutyai sūtram /
body.translated_text: Now, the sūtra on <s>apahnutī</s> (concealment).

body.text: viṣayāpahnave 'pahnutiḥ || 20 ||
body.translated_text: The denial of the subject is <s>apahnutī</s> (concealment). (RuAss 20)

body.text:
nanu mukhaṃ na bhavatīti viṣayāpahnavamātre satyapi nāpahnutirityato 'dhikāraṃ smārayati-vastvantarapratītirityeveti /
ataḥ prakṛtaniṣedha puraskāreṇa aprakṛtasamarthanamapahnutirityarthaḥ /
tathāhi kāvyaprakāśakṛt- "prakṛtaṃ yanniṣidhyānyat sādhyate sā tvapahnutiḥ /
" nanu yadi sādṛśyādvastvantarapratītirihāpi ko viśeṣaḥ tarhyasya bhrāntimata ityata āha-prakāntānapahvavetyādi /
prakrāntaṃ prakṛtam /
tasya hyatrāpahnuvaḥ /
bhrāntimatyanapahnava iti viśeṣaḥ /
ullekhe tu na prakṛtānapahnavamātraṃ viśeṣaḥ kintu anekadhāgrahaṇamapi jñeyam /

children.translated_text: The word '<s>idam</s>' (this) is an adverbial modifier of the action.
That this is the <s>apahnutī</s>-statement is by virtue of the distinction from '<s>prakrāntānapahnava</s>' (non-denial of the contextual)—such is the meaning.
To extract the definition, he says '<s>āropaprastāvāt</s>' etc.
'The occasion of superimposition' means from <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) onward.

body.translated_text: Now, even when there is mere denial of the subject—'this is not a face'—it is not yet <s>apahnutī</s>; therefore he reminds of the governing rule: '<s>vastvantarapratītir ityeva</s>' (there must be the apprehension of another thing). Therefore, <s>apahnutī</s> is the establishment of something non-contextual preceded by the denial of the contextual—such is the meaning. As the author of the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s> states: 'When the contextual is denied and something else is established, that is <s>apahnutī</s>.' Now, if here too the apprehension of another thing arises from similarity, what distinction is there then from <s>bhrāntimān</s> (delusion)?—to address this he says '<s>prakrāntānapahnave</s>' etc. '<s>Prakrānta</s>' means 'the contextual.' Its denial occurs here [in <s>apahnutī</s>]. The distinction is that in <s>bhrāntimān</s> there is no denial. In <s>ullekha</s>, however, the distinguishing feature is not merely the non-denial of the contextual, but also the manifold apprehension—this should be known.

children.translated_text: 'The counterpart of the hare (<s>śaśaka</s>)'—thus.

children.text: apahnotumiṣyasya śaśakasya yaḥ prativastubhūta ulkāpātakiṇaḥ tasyaivāropo nyāyyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of the hare whose concealment is desired, the counterpart—namely the mark of a meteor-fall (<s>ulkāpātakiṇa</s>)—its superimposition alone is appropriate.
But not of the moon which possesses it; therefore the syntactic connection does not hold.

children.text: itthaṃ lakṣaṇopapanno 'pi alaṅkāro doṣānuviddhaḥsan ābhāsī bhavatīti vyutpādya samyagudājihīrṣurāha-tattu yatheti //
children.translated_text: Thus, having demonstrated that even a figure possessing its proper definition becomes an apparent example when tainted by a fault, wishing to illustrate a correct example, he says '<s>tat tu yathā</s>' etc.

body.translated_text: To show the variety of its modes, he says '<s>tasya trayī</s>' etc. '<s>Trayī</s>' means 'of three kinds'—such is the meaning. The variety lies in the compositional texture: the triplicity is analyzed. He distinguishes the three kinds: '<s>apahnavapūrvaka</s>' etc. '<s>Chadma</s>' and similar words—<s>chadma</s>, <s>chala</s>, <s>kaitava</s>, <s>nibha</s>, and the like—by these too, only the negative sense is conveyed. Then what is the distinctive delight in the third kind?—to address this he says '<s>pūrvaka</s>' etc. '<s>Yad etat</s>'—'it is not so to me'—the denial of the contextual; in the second half, the establishment of the non-contextual. Although this is <s>apahnutī</s>, still because it is tainted by a fault, it is an apparent example (<s>udāharaṇābhāsa</s>)—to address this he says '<s>atra indavasya</s>' etc.

body.text: pūrṇondoriti /

children.translated_text: Anger born from a perceived or heard offense is called <s>māna</s> (indignation/amorous sulking).

children.text: tenonnaddhaḥ utsikto janaḥ śṛṅgārī lokaḥ tasyābhimānaḥsāntvāsahiṣṇutā /
children.translated_text: One puffed up, elated with that, is a <s>śṛṅgārī</s> (amorous person); his pride is the intolerance of conciliation.
'<s>Hevāka</s>' means disdain.

children.text: atra na maṇḍalam api tu ātapatramevetyanvayo ghaṭate ayamapahnavapūrvaka āropaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here the syntactic connection is: 'not a disc, but an umbrella'—this is denial-preceded superimposition.

body.translated_text: 'Of the full moon'—thus.

body.text: āropapūrvakamudāharati-vilasadamareti //
body.translated_text: He illustrates superimposition-preceded [concealment]: '<s>vilasad-amara</s>' etc.

children.translated_text: By '<s>sārdhaṃ dhāvatām</s>' (running along with), the spread of fame to that region is simultaneously indicated.
'Under the guise of pearls'—

children.text: ambhaḥ kaṇairbhaṣṭamityatra hi na muktāphalāni, api tu ambhaḥ kaṇā eveti pratītiḥ /
children.translated_text: In '<s>ambhaḥ kaṇair bhaṣṭam</s>' (sprinkled with water drops), the apprehension is: 'not pearls, but water drops.'

children.text: itthamevāpahnutim utprekṣāṅgatvena pratipipādayuṣurupakṣipati-atra śūnyaṃ ityasya ityādi //
children.translated_text: Thus, to those who would present <s>apahnutī</s> as a subordinate element of <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), he raises an objection: '<s>atra śūnyam</s> <s>ityasya</s>' etc.

body.translated_text: '<s>Saṃyama</s>' means restraint of the mind. By that, 'made low' means 'subdued.' Here, 'he sits upon the groves of eyes'—not 'he dwells on the peacock'—thus it is superimposition-preceded. '<s>Udbhrānta</s>'—

children.translated_text: In the reading '<s>manye marāvi</s>' etc., by the force of the word '<s>manye</s>' (I think), it is <s>utprekṣā</s>.
But by the word '<s>chadma</s>' (guise), it is <s>apahnutī</s>; and this will be subordinate to <s>utprekṣā</s>.

children.text: itthamutprekṣāṅgatvaṃ na kevalaṃ tṛtīyabhedasyaiva, yāvatā pūrvabhedadvayasyāpi saṃbhavatītyāha ahaṃ tvindumityādi //
children.translated_text: Thus, the status of being subordinate to <s>utprekṣā</s> is possible not only for the third kind, but for the first two kinds as well—he says '<s>ahaṃ tv indum</s>' etc.
The mention of sentence-division is to manifest the first two kinds.
Thus, <s>apahnutī</s> in all three forms has been indicated as subordinate to <s>utprekṣā</s>.

children.text: nanu cchralādiprayoge 'pyapahnavāropapaurvāparyaviparyayanibandhanaṃ vaicitryaṃ kiṃ nocyata ityata āha-etasminnapīti //
children.translated_text: Now, why is the variety based on the reversal of the order of denial and superimposition not stated even when words like <s>chadma</s> (guise) are used?—to address this he says '<s>etasmin api</s>' etc.
