tasya phalasya yadeva lokasthityā kāraṇaṃ , tadevotprekṣaṇanimittam /
taccennopādīyeta, tadevotprekṣyamāṇaṃ phalaṃ kasya phalatayoktaṃ syāt /
ataḥ phalotprekṣāyāṃ nimittopādānaniyama eva /
tadidamudāhṛtya darśayati-rathasthitānāmiti /
atrottaradiśasturagotpattibhūmitvāt tadgamanaṃ purātanaturaṅgaparivartane hetuḥ /
tadevotprekṣaṇanimittam /
tadanupādāne parivartamānaṃ utprekṣyamāṇaṃ kasya phalaṃ syāt /
tadidamabhipretyāha-atra parivartanasyetyādi /
anenāśīcilidhatvena dṛṣṭeṣu prabhedeṣu punaḥ keṣāñcit pātodarśitaḥ /
tathāhi-upāttanimittā ye ṣoḍaṣabhedāsteṣāṃ pratisvaṃ hetusvarūpa phalotprekṣaṇarūpatve aṣṭacatvāriṃśat /
dravye hetuphalotprekṣā pāte 'ṣṭa kahāniriti catvāriṃśat /
anupāttanimittatve tu ṣoḍaśakehetuphalarūpatābhāvāt svarupotprekṣaikarūpataiveti ṣoḍaśaiva /
ataḥ tatṣaṭpañcāśadeva prabhedāḥ /
yaditthamiyamutprekṣā atisūkṣmekṣikayā prapañcitā /
tatra-hetumāha-tadasāvityādi /
kakṣyāvibhāgo jātiguṇādirūpatayā sthitaḥ /
pracurasthito 'pi anākulanyāyatayā prabhūtavṛttirapi /
lakṣye duḥravadhāratvāt uttānadhiyāṃ lakṣyayojanāntamaśakyādhigamatvāt(na)prapañcita ityarthaḥ /
atha manyepramukhasya śabdasya saṃbhāvanādyotakatve 'pi tatprayogamātreṇotprekṣābhramo na kārya iti vyutpādayati-asyāścetyādi /
utprekṣāsāmagrayabhāva iti /
aprakṛtagataguṇakriyābhisambandhāt aprakṛtatvena prakṛtasaṃbhāvanamutprekṣāsāmagrī /

children.translated_text: In its absence, [what appears to be <s>utprekṣā</s>] is merely conjecture — simply speculation expressed by the word <s>nūnam</s> (surely).
He recalls this: 'as was illustrated previously...' etc.
Here are summary verses: 'Through the connection with a quality or action, [supposing] the contextual in the form of the non-contextual —'
'That supposition would be <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy); it is expressed through the initial [particles]; otherwise [it is] suggested.'

body.translated_text:
'For a day' — the second case-ending is used in the sense of absolute conjunction.
He reveals the implied <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy): 'here, in "it does not end"...' etc.
Since the principle is well known, fearing prolixity he says: 'thus in other varieties...' etc.
Since <s>utprekṣā</s> can also occur based on the sense-level, caused by equivocal words (<s>śliṣṭa-śabda</s>), in the domain of properties — he illustrates what was indicated: 'equivocal word...' etc.
'<s>Ananya</s>' — the well-known generous one, that is, a mode of singing.
'<s>Mārgaṇāḥ</s>' means arrows, or suppliants.
For connecting the characteristics, he says: 'here, in the domain of properties...' etc.
The property is the becoming-an-object of arrows; the cognition rests in supposition alone, so the equivocation does not obstruct <s>utprekṣā</s>.
'<s>Kastūrī</s>' — [example follows].
'<s>Rolambā</s>' means bees.
'<s>Aṅka</s>' means the border or edge.
'<s>Sthāsaka</s>' means a song or musical piece.
He demonstrates the simile-initial nature: 'here, although...' etc.
The meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is: 'Some teachers [say] that the <s>kvip</s> suffix [comes] after all nominal stems in the sense of comparison.'
Here, due to the greatness of the <s>kvip</s> suffix, even the comparison that is initially perceived culminates in supposition.
Since the rule that the radiance of the throat takes the form of a <s>tilaka</s> mark etc. is not established, the <s>tilaka</s>-form too could sometimes exist in the comparison-element — but it has supposition as its vital essence, not actuality.
Therefore it culminates in <s>utprekṣā</s>.
With this intention, he says: 'nevertheless, because of the standard of comparison...' etc.
Because of the propriety of mere supposition — since the standard of comparison (the <s>tilaka</s> etc.) could possibly exist in the contextual subject (the form of throat-radiance).
Upon the arising of supposition, <s>utprekṣā</s> (fancy) arises.
Now, to show that even when a suffix other than the comparison-suffix is used, the simile-initial nature holds — he says: 'as also...' etc.
In '<s>keyūrāyitam</s>' (made into an armlet) too, due to the greatness of the <s>kyaṅ</s> suffix, the perception of comparison with an armlet etc. [arises].
Since there is no rule that [the subject] must behave exactly like an armlet etc., it culminates in <s>utprekṣā</s> through supposition of such-ness.
Now, intending [to say] that wherever the comparison-element is not actually established but comes through the poet's imagination, all simile — though initially perceived through the greatness of the simile-indicating word — culminates as <s>utprekṣā</s>, he says: 'and this...' etc.
He states the reason for not elaborating: 'thus...' etc.
'Having gone to the shore' — the hurried gait is the cause of the foam's outbreak.
Here, from the word '<s>iva</s>' (like), the laughter is [merely] supposed.
What the author of the <s>Vyaktiviveka</s> says regarding this topic — 'by words like <s>iva</s> alone the non-reality of the contextual meaning is perceived; words like <s>chala</s> (pretense) are therefore redundant' — that is shallow.
For in such a domain, even without the use of words like <s>chala</s>, the non-reality or unreality of the contextual meaning is not understood.
Rather, it serves merely as a reason for <s>utprekṣā</s>.
As, for instance, in the reading '<s>phenāparaṃparābhiḥ</s>' (with successions of foam) in this very [verse].
Therefore, the variety of <s>utprekṣā</s> characterized by concealment (<s>sāpahnava</s>) depends solely on the use of words like <s>chala</s>.
With this intention, he says: 'here, by the word <s>iva</s>...' etc.
Now, for the purpose of elaborating <s>utprekṣā</s> itself, he explains that through the extraction of particular words that serve as seeds of various figures, ornamental variety emerges: 'another, <s>iva</s>...' etc.
Even without the word '<s>apara</s>' (another), <s>Pākaśāsana</s> (<s>Indra</s>) is perceived as established — so it is mere simile.
But with the use of that word, the contextual king himself is determined as 'another <s>Pākaśāsana</s>' [through identification].
And since identification is accomplished by the word <s>iva</s>, it is <s>utprekṣā</s> alone.
In the removal of the word <s>iva</s>, the perception of the predominance of <s>rūpaka</s>-type non-difference [arises].
Thus, wishing to explain that in this [figure] filled with manifold variety, in some aspects there is necessarily expressed meaning, while in others there is free play — he first explains the <s>hetu-utprekṣā</s> (fancy of cause): 'thus of this kind...' etc.
Belonging to the contextual means belonging to the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison).
The property whose cause is fancied — that property, through the force of identification and through the force of non-difference attribution — is assumed as non-different and the basis of the <s>utprekṣā</s>; it necessarily becomes expressed.
Two rules should be traced: its assumption of non-difference with the property of the <s>upamāna</s> (standard), and [the fact that] the expressedness is [part of the rule].
If it were not so, the fancied cause would be like a painting without a wall — he says: 'otherwise, to whom...' etc.
He makes this arrangement enter the heart through examples: 'as, not seeing...' etc.
Here, the cheeks are contextual; the property belonging to them is emaciation; the cause — seeing [each other] — is fancied.
And in that fancying, it is not mere cheek-emaciation that is the basis, but the emaciation that occurs in the world between those who do not see each other — that, being identified as non-different, is itself fancied; and the result is the cause characterized as seeing.
With this intention, he says: 'here, of the cheeks...' etc.
'And that is different' — the meaning is: at the stage of the result, it is identified as non-different.
Emaciation is indeed the result due to not-seeing — and in that regard, the cause is the impelling factor in the fancying of the cause.
The meaning is: the coming of emaciation to those who do not see each other — [the contextual emaciation] is identified as non-different with that.
This is the <s>hetu-utprekṣā</s> characterized by action that has the nature of non-existence-attribution.
The same principle applies to <s>hetu-utprekṣā</s> characterized by existence-attribution — he says: 'thus, it is seen...' etc.
Here too, the silence (<s>maunitva</s>) of the anklet is fancied as the cause of sorrow.
In that fancying, worldly sorrow-silence, identified as non-different, is the basis — the silence of the anklet is the cause and the fancying of sorrow is the result.
This procedure is uniform everywhere in <s>hetu-utprekṣā</s> — he says: 'thus everywhere...' etc.
Now, in <s>svarūpa-utprekṣā</s> (fancy of nature), sometimes the subject is identified as being another subject.
Sometimes, however, it is the property itself [that is identified] as belonging to another subject.
In both cases, the causal element is sometimes expressed.
Sometimes it is not — he begins to analyze: 'in <s>svarūpa-utprekṣā</s>, where the subject...' etc.
'May he protect you' — thus.
Here, because the similarity between the moon-crescent and the skull-sprout is not established;
the characteristic of crookedness is verbally adopted; but in 'like a wave of the ocean of passion,' the agitating-capacity is well-known, so it is not adopted.
Now, he shows the adoption and non-adoption of the cause in the case of a property identified as belonging to [another] subject: 'and where the property itself...' etc.
'Having received the consecration' — the connection is with 'the earth of enemies.'
Here he analyzes the supposition of the property and the adoption of the cause: 'here, the earth-belonging-ness...' etc.
'As if smearing' — he analyzes the non-adoption of the cause: 'here, the darkness-belonging...' etc.
But should not the covering be fancied as smearing, for the sake of variety in the fancying of properties? He responds: 'but in covering etc....' etc.
Another cause would have to be sought — i.e., just as in fancying smearing, covering is understood as the cause, similarly in fancying covering, no other cause is grasped.
Therefore, two faults would result: the fabrication of what is not grasped and the abandonment of what is grasped — this is the purport.
He raises another objection: 'and not of the subject...' etc.
If covering alone is the subject of the fancying, its not-being-understood is indeed inappropriate.
The reason: 'because of its being the substrate of the fancied' — i.e., fancied means the fancier [the cause]; because of being the substrate of that, because it is appropriate to express only what is contextual.
Therefore, he concludes that smearing alone is fancied: 'therefore, as stated...' etc.
Now, he begins [to say] that in <s>phala-utprekṣā</s> (fancy of result), non-adoption of the cause is impossible: 'in <s>phala-utprekṣā</s>...' etc.
The very thing that is the cause of that result in the ordinary course of the world — that itself is the basis of the fancying.
If that were not adopted, the result being fancied — of what would it be stated as a result?
Therefore, in <s>phala-utprekṣā</s>, the adoption of the cause is mandatory.
He illustrates this with an example: 'of those standing in the chariot...' etc.
Here, because the northern direction is the birthplace of horses, going there is the cause of the exchange of old horses.
That itself is the basis of the fancying.
Without its adoption, the exchange being fancied — of what would it be the result?
With this intention, he says: 'here, of the exchange...' etc.
By this, the falling of certain [sub-types] into previously indicated varieties [with the benedictive etc.] is shown.
Thus: the sixteen varieties with adopted cause, each taking the form of hetu-, svarūpa-, and phala-utprekṣā, make forty-eight.
In substance, hetu- and phala-utprekṣā falling [into] eight [variations] each — [gives] forty.
But without adopted cause, since the sixteen [basic types] lack the hetu- and phala-forms, there is only the single form of svarūpa-utprekṣā — so only sixteen.
Therefore, the total is fifty-six varieties.
Since this <s>utprekṣā</s> has been elaborated with exceedingly subtle analysis —
he states the reason: 'because this...' etc.
The division into classes exists in the form of genus, quality, etc.
Although standing abundantly — through the orderliness of non-confusion, having extensive operation —
because it is difficult to determine in the [actual] instances — because for those of ordinary intellect the connection of the final characteristic-application is impossible to ascertain — it was not elaborated — this is the meaning.
Now, he explains that even when a word like <s>manye</s> (I think) indicates supposition, mere use of that word should not create the delusion that it is <s>utprekṣā</s>: 'and of this...' etc.
The absence of the aggregate of <s>utprekṣā</s>: the connection with a quality or action belonging to the non-contextual — i.e., the supposition of the contextual as non-contextual through [that connection] — is the aggregate of <s>utprekṣā</s>.

children.translated_text: 'That [<s>utprekṣā</s>] is fourfold through the fancying of genus, action, quality, and substance.'
'Through the nature of attributing existence and non-existence to genus etc., it becomes eightfold again.'
'Through the quality- and action-causality, it should be known as sixteenfold.'
'And thirty-two, through the adoption or non-adoption of the cause, standing otherwise.'

children.text: hetau svarūpe cotprekṣye phale ṣaṇṇāvatiḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In the fancying of cause, nature, and result — ninety-six again.'
'Due to the impossibility of substance-cause-result nature, the division falls away.'
'Similarly, in the implied [<s>utprekṣā</s>], there is no adoption of the cause,'
'Nor is there nature [fancying] by those varieties; therefore this [total] would be less.'
'Sometimes, through the equivocal attribution of the property-element, this [<s>utprekṣā</s>] is not obstructed.'
'This [<s>utprekṣā</s>] may also be simile-initial and may also have concealment.'

body.text:
athotprekṣāṃ nigamayan atiśayoktiṃ saṅgatipuraskāreṇa prastauti-evamadhyavasāyasyeti /
siddhatva iti /
adhyavasitasya viṣayiṇaḥ prādhānye adhyavasāyasya siddhatvam /
atha sūtram-
body.translated_text:
Now, concluding <s>utprekṣā</s>, he introduces <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) with a connection-prelude: 'thus, of the identification...' etc.
'Established-ness' — when the identified object (the <s>viṣayin</s>) predominates, the identification is established.
Now the <s>sūtra</s> —

body.text: adhyavasitaprādhānye tvatiśayoktiḥ || 22 ||
body.translated_text: When the identified [object] predominates, that is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole). || <s>RuAss</s> 22 ||

body.text:
utprekṣātiśayoktyoḥ viṣayaṃ vibhaktumāha-adhyavasāye trayamityādi /
svarūpamadhyavasānaṃ vyāpārātmakam /
viṣayaḥ prakṛtor'thaḥ viṣayī tvaprakṛtaḥ /
tatrādhyavasāyasvarūpam utprekṣāprastāve vivecitam /
pratītivaiśadyāya smārayati-viṣayasya hītyādi /
antarnītatve nigīrṇatve /
tatrotprekṣāviṣayaṃ vibhajati-śādhyatve svarūpaprādhānyamiti /
atiśayoktiviṣayaṃ vibhajati-siddhatve adhyavasitaprādhānyamiti /
adhyavasito guṇīkṛtādhyavasāno viṣayī /
viṣayastu prādhānyaṃ nārhatītyāha-viṣayaprādhānyamiti /
naiva saṃbhavatīti viṣayasya /
viṣayiṇānigīrṇasvarūpapratītireva tirodhīyate /
prādhānayasaṃbhavaḥ kuta iti bhāvaḥ /
atiśayoktilakṣaṇaṃ nigamayati-adhyavasitaprādhānye ceti /
tadbhedānuddiśati-tasyāścetyādi /
krameṇodāharaṇāni-kamalamanambhasīti /
atra mukhanayanagātralakṣaṇānviṣayān nigīrya kamalakuvalayakanakalatālakṣaṇā viṣayiṇaḥ tadabhedenādhyavasitāḥ /

children.translated_text: He explains the non-difference within difference: 'here, of the face etc....' etc.
'<s>Aṇṇaṃ saḍahe</s>' (Prākrit) — thus.
'Another beauty, and also some other aspect of appearance and complexion —'
'O dark one, of the general <s>Prajāpati</s> (Creator), is not even a line.'

body.translated_text:
To distinguish the domains of <s>utprekṣā</s> and <s>atiśayokti</s>, he says: 'in identification, there are three [elements]...' etc.
The nature of identification is operational.
The <s>viṣaya</s> (object/subject) is the contextual meaning; the <s>viṣayin</s> (possessor/identifier) is the non-contextual.
Of these, the nature of identification was analyzed in the <s>utprekṣā</s> discussion.
For clarity of understanding, he reminds: 'for of the subject...' etc.
'When internalized' means when absorbed.
He distinguishes the domain of <s>utprekṣā</s>: 'when in the state of being established, the predominance of the nature [obtains]' — thus.
He distinguishes the domain of <s>atiśayokti</s>: 'when established, the predominance of the identified [obtains]' — thus.
The identified — i.e., the <s>viṣayin</s> whose identification has been subordinated.
But the <s>viṣaya</s> (subject) does not merit predominance — he says: 'the predominance of the subject...' etc.
'Is not possible at all' — of the subject.
For the very perception of the subject's own nature, which has been absorbed by the <s>viṣayin</s>, is concealed.
How can there be any possibility of predominance? — this is the purport.
He concludes the definition of <s>atiśayokti</s>: 'when the identified predominates...' etc.
He indicates its varieties: 'and of that...' etc.
Examples in order: 'a lotus in waterless [ground]' — thus.
Here, the subjects characterized as face, eyes, and body are absorbed, and the identifiers characterized as lotus, <s>kuvalaya</s> (blue lotus), and gold-vine are identified as non-different with them.

body.text:
laḍahatvaṃ prauḍhatvam /
abhede bhedaṃ darśayati-atra laḍahetyādi /
atrābhede bhedo dharmaniṣṭha ekaviṣayo darśitaḥ /

children.translated_text: To show it as both subject-based and multi-subject, he says: 'as also...' etc.
'<s>Ṇārāṇotti</s>' (Prākrit) — thus.
'By those of mature age [he is seen as] <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; by young women as the beloved of <s>Śrī</s>;'
'By young girls again, with curiosity, he is seen just as he is.'

body.translated_text:
'<s>Laḍahatva</s>' means maturity/boldness.
He shows the difference within non-difference: 'here, maturity...' etc.
Here, the difference within non-difference is shown as property-based and single-subject.

body.text:
ityatra pariṇātavayaskānāṃ śrīvallabhatvābhede 'pi nārāyaṇa iti (bhe)dena dṛṣṭastathaivābhiruceḥ /
taruṇīnāṃ nārāyaṇatvābhede 'pi śrīvallabha ityeva, tathaivārthitvāt /
bālānāṃ tu yatkiñciditi nūtanaṃ vastu draṣṭavyamityeva, tathā vyutpatteḥ /
yadvā pratyekaṃ samastā rucyarthitvavyutpattayobhedadṛṣṭau nimittaṃ prapañcitam ullekhaprastāve /
tadidamabhisandhāyāha-atrābhinnasyāpīti /
abhinnasya dharmiṇā iti śeṣaḥ /
viṣayavibhāgena /
pariṇatavayaskādi(nā) /
lāvaṇyetyatra sambandhe 'sambandha- /
atraikanirmātṛniṣṭatayā dharmasambandhe 'sambandhaḥ /
atha bhinnanirmātṛniṣṭhatayāpi darśayitumāha-yathā veti /
asyāḥsargeti /
śṛṅgāraikarasa iti pratyekamabhisaṃbadhyate /
puṣpaṃ pravāleli /
atra puṣpapravālādikayoḥ sākṣādasambandhe 'pi yadīti saṃbhāvanayā sambandhaḥ /
puṣpakāle pravālatvāpagamāt /
na ca mantavyaṃ saṃbhāvanāyāṃ vyāpāraprādhānyāt atrotprekṣaiveyamiti /
tato 'nukuryāditi samanvayavākye adhyavasitaprādhānyāt /
ata utprekṣānugṛhīteyamatiśayoktiḥ /
taditamabhisandhāyāha-atra saṃbhāvanayā saṃbandha iti /
athotprekṣāgrahaṇamantareṇāpi asaṃbandhe saṃbandhamudārahati-dāho 'mbhaḥ prasṛtimiti /
atra dāhabāṣpaśvāsavapuṣāmambhaḥ prasṛtiṃ pacatvapraṇālocitatvadīpakalikāpreṅkholanapāṇḍimamajjaneṣu saṃbandhābhāve api siddhatvenoktiḥ /
tadetadāha-atra dāhādīnāmityādi /
kāryakāraṇapaurvāparyavidhvaṃse dvaividhyamāha-kāryakāraṇetyādi /
viparyayaḥ kāryasya pūrvakālabhāvitā /
hṛdayamiti /
atra hṛdayasya dayaṭitādhiṣṭhānaṃ kusumacāpabāṇādhiṣṭhānasya kāraṇam /
kāraṇañca niyatapūrvakālabhāvi /
tadihānyathopanyastamiti paurvāparyaviparyayaḥ /
aviraleti /
nīpaḥ kadambaḥ /
prāvṛḍayanaṃ pathikagehinīmṛtikāraṇam /
atra tvāyāto mṛtā iti niṣṭhābhyāṃ tayoḥsamakālatā /
nanu bhede 'bhedādikatha namasaṅgatam ityata āha-eṣu pañcasviti /
lokātikrāntagocaraṃlokātiśā yitvalakṣaṇaṃ gocarayatītyarthaḥ /
ato bhede 'bhedarūpo mukhyārtho na vivakṣita itiyāvat /
nanu bhede 'bhedādhyavasāyo lakṣaṇamatiśayokteḥ /
tadabhede bheda ityādāvavyāpakamityata āha-atra cātiśayākhyamityādinā /
yadiha bhede 'bhedādirūpāyā atiśayoktinimittabhūtaṃ prayojakamatiśayākhyaṃ phalaṃ tatrābhedādhyavasāyo, na tu phalinoḥ /
taditamupadarśayati-tathā hītyādi /
vadanādīnāṃ yadvastuvṛttasiddhaṃ saundaryaṃ tatkavisamarpitena kamalādisaundaryeṇa sahābhedenādhyavasitaṃ sadbhede 'bhedādivacanasya nimittaṃ kamalamukhādikayorabhedādhyavasāyo yojayituṃ śakyaḥ /
tathāsati avyātpidoṣaḥ syādityata āha-abhede bheda ityādi /
ādiśabdāt sambandhe 'sambandhaparigrahaḥ /
prakāreṣviti /
bahuvacanaṃ tadavāntarabhedaparam /
abhede vāstave yadā bhedakathanaṃ na hi tadā phalinorabhedādhyavasāyaḥ /
phalaṃ tu tatrāpyabhedenaivādhyavasīyata ityata āha-aṇṇaṃ laḍahattaṇaaṃ ityādāviti /
aṇṇaṃ laḍahattaṇaamityādau hi yat vastu tasmiddhaṃ laḍahatvaṃ yaccānyatvena kavisamarpitaṃ sātiśayaṃ, na khalu tayorbhedaḥ kaścit /
kintu samānyaprajāpatinirmāṇakavisamarpitanirmāṇayoreva phalinorbhedaḥ /
ayaṃ nyāyaḥsambandhe 'sambandhaḥ ityatrāpi sama ityāha-evamanyatreti /
tatrāpi khalu "lāvaṇyadraviṇe"tyādau vedhaso lāvaṇyardraviṇasambandhe 'pyasaṃbandhaḥ kevalaṃ na punastanvyā naisargikalāvaṇyakavisamarpitavedhaḥsambandhi lāvaṇyayorasaṃbandhaḥ /
eva "masyāḥ sargavidhā"vityatrāpi jñeyam /
niyamato lakṣaṇabhūtamadhyavasitaprādhānyaṃ phalābhiprāyeṇaivetyāha-tadabhiprāyeṇaivetyādi /

children.translated_text: Now, wishing to further analyze the mode characterized by cause and effect, he allays the doubt of repetition — 'in the fivefold mode...' etc.

children.text: kāryatāśrayatvāt tatrāpi saṅgatiḥ prapañcārthatvāt nānarthakyamiti sarvamavadātam /
children.translated_text: Because it pertains to the effect, there is connection there too; because it serves elaboration, there is no purposelessness — thus everything is clear.
The determination of non-difference pertains to the result, in the figure called <s>atiśaya</s> (hyperbole),
but non-difference does not fail to be established in the result-producers there.

body.translated_text:
Here, for those of mature age, although there is no difference in being dear to <s>Śrī</s> (Prosperity), they perceive through difference as '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' — such is their inclination.
For young women, although there is no difference in being <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, they perceive as 'dear to <s>Śrī</s>' only — such is their desire.
But for children, whatever is new is to be seen — such is their understanding.
Alternatively, for each of the three — inclination, desire, and understanding — difference of perception is the cause; this has been elaborated in the discussion of <s>ullekha</s> (multiple perception).
With this in mind he says: 'here, even of what is non-different...' etc.
'Of what is non-different from the qualified' — this is to be supplied.
'By the division of the domain' — by the distinction of viewers such as the mature etc.
In '<s>lāvaṇya</s>' (charm) — there is non-relation within a relation.
Here, by the characteristic of belonging to a single creator, there is non-relation within the relation of properties.
Now, to show this even when the creators are different, he says: 'as in...' etc.
'Of this creation' — '<s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) alone as <s>rasa</s>' applies to each individually.
'Flower, coral-shoot' — here, although there is no direct relation between flower and coral-shoot, a relation is established through supposition ('if').
Because during the flower season, the coral-shoot status is gone.
Nor should one think that since supposition predominates in operation, this is merely <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy);
because in the continuation sentence 'would then imitate,' the predominance is of the determined meaning (<s>adhyavasita</s>).
Therefore this is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) aided by <s>utprekṣā</s>.
With this in mind he says: 'here, a relation through supposition...' etc.
Now, even without recourse to <s>utprekṣā</s>, he illustrates non-relation within relation: '<s>dāha</s> (burning), water-stream...' etc.
Here, for burning, tears, sighs, and pallor — in their relations with water-stream, cooking, wind-channel-fanning, and immersion respectively — although there is no actual relation, the statement is made as if established.
This he states: 'here, of burning etc....' etc.
He shows the twofold nature when the sequential order of cause and effect is disrupted: 'cause and effect...' etc.
Reversal means the prior temporal existence of the effect.
'The heart' — here, the heart's being the locus of <s>Dayiṭā</s> (beloved) is the cause of the <s>Kusumacāpa</s> (Flower-bow, i.e., <s>Kāma</s>)'s arrows having a locus.
And the cause invariably exists prior in time.
But here it is presented otherwise — thus it is a reversal of temporal sequence.
'Dense' — <s>nīpa</s> is the <s>kadamba</s> tree.
The rainy season's arrival is the cause of the traveler's wife's death.
But here, by the two past participles 'arrived' and 'died,' their simultaneity is indicated.
Now, how is non-difference in difference etc. coherent? — He answers: 'in these five...' etc.
'It makes the supramundane accessible' — meaning it produces the characteristic of surpassing the world.
Therefore, in difference, the primary meaning of non-difference is not intended — this is the purport.
Now, the definition of <s>atiśayokti</s> is the determination of non-difference where there is difference.
Then in 'non-difference in difference' and the like, it would be too narrow — he addresses this: 'here, the one called <s>atiśaya</s> (excess)...' etc.
The result that is called '<s>atiśaya</s>' (excess/hyperbole) — which is the cause and produces the figure of <s>atiśayokti</s> — in that, the determination of non-difference pertains to the result, not to the two result-producers.
He illustrates this: 'for thus...' etc.
The actual beauty of the face etc. and the beauty of the lotus etc. attributed by the poet — when determined as non-different despite the real difference — the determination of non-difference between the face and lotus etc. can be applied as the cause of the statement of non-difference in difference.
Were it otherwise, the fault of non-pervasion would arise — he says: 'non-difference in difference...' etc.
By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), non-relation within relation is also included.
'In the modes' — the plural refers to their sub-varieties.
In actual non-difference, when there is a statement of difference, then the determination of non-difference does not pertain to the result-producers.
But the result there too is determined as non-difference only — he says: 'in "<s>aṇṇaṃ laḍahattaṇaaṃ</s>" etc...'
In '<s>aṇṇaṃ laḍahattaṇaaṃ</s>' etc., whatever is the object and whatever charmingness is attributed by the poet with exaggeration — between these there is no difference at all.
Rather, the difference is only between the two result-producers: the creation by the general <s>Prajāpati</s> and the creation attributed by the poet.
This same principle applies equally to 'non-relation within relation' — he says: 'likewise elsewhere...' etc.
There too, in '<s>lāvaṇyadraviṇe</s>' (the wealth of charm) etc., although there is a relation of the Creator with the wealth of charm, there is non-relation; but the non-relation is not between the woman's natural charm and the charm attributed by the poet as related to the Creator.
The same should be understood in '<s>asyāḥ sargavidhāv</s>' (in the creation of this one) etc.
That the predominance of determination, which constitutes the definition, is intended with reference to the result only — he says: 'with that very intention...' etc.

body.text:
athādhyavasāyamūlamalaṅkāradvayaṃ nigamayan dharmāntaramadhicikīrṣurāha-evamadhyavasāyāśrayeṇetyādi /
gamyamānaupamyāśrayeṣvapi yannyāyātprādhānyamarhati taddvayamadhikaroti-tatrāpi padārthetyādinā /
tatra tulyayogitārthaṃ sūtram /
body.translated_text:
Now, concluding the two figures based on determination and wishing to treat a different property, he says: 'thus, through the basis of determination...' etc.
Even in those based on perceived similarity, he treats the two that by logical reasoning deserve primacy — 'there too, through the referent...' etc.
For that purpose, the <s>sūtra</s> on <s>Tulyayogitā</s> (equal connection):

body.text: aupamyasya gamyatve padārthagatatvena prastutānāmaprastutānāṃ vā samānadharmābhisambandhe tulyayogitā || 23 ||
body.translated_text: When the similarity is implied, and the connection of the contextual or non-contextual subjects with a common property is through the referent level — that is <s>Tulyayogitā</s> (equal connection). || <s>RuAss</s> 23 ||

body.text:
aupamyasya gamyatve padārthagatatvenetyadhikāradvayam, anyattu lakṣaṇaṃ vyācaṣṭe-ivādyaprayoga ityādi /
prākaraṇikānāmaprākaraṇikānāṃ veti viṣayadvayam /
guṇakriyā ceti dharmadvayam /
ata ścāturvidhyamanusandheyam /
prākaraṇikeṣu guṇābhaisaṃbandhaḥ, kriyābhisambandhaśca /
aprākaraṇikeṣu tatheti /
samānaguṇa kriyāsaṃbandho hi tulyayogi(tā) /
tāmimāṃ niruktimāviṣkaroti-anvitārtheti /
anvitārthā anvarthā /
sajjeti /
tāmimāṃ niruktimāviṣkaroti-anvitārtheti /
anvitārthā anvarthā /
sajjeti /
dināni sajjānāmātapatrāṇāṃ prakarairañcitāni /
padmāni tu sajjātānāṃ sujātānāṃ patrāṇām /
pāṭaletyekatka varṇāḥ, anvatra tu puṣpam /
prākaraṇikārthaviṣayatāṃ kriyābhisaṃbandhaṃ ca darśayati-atra ṛtuvarṇanetyādi /
ṛturgrīṣmaḥ /
prākaraṇikeṣu guṇābhisandhāyāha-evaṃ guṇe 'pīti /
yogapaṭṭa iti /
atra tapaḥ prastāvādyogapaṭṭādīnāṃ prakṛtatvam /
ucitatvaṃ guṇasvabhāvābhimānarūpatayābhisaṃbadhyate, yadyucitāni taducyatāmityākṣepāt /
anena guṇakriyayorbhāvābhāvābhimānarūpaṃ vaicitryamapyāsūtritam /
dhāvattvavaśveti /
aśvapṛtanāyāḥsakāśāt gūrñjaranṛpasya bhagrasya mukhe patitaṃ rajaḥ /
kayāpi sānukampayā tanvyā pramṛṣṭam /
yaśastu tavāsilatayā /
aprākaraṇikaviṣayaṃ kriyābhisaṃbadhaṃ darśayati-atra gūrjaraṃ pratītyādi /
gūrjarāpekṣayāhikayāpīti nirdeśāt tanvyā aprākaraṇikatvam /
asilatāyāstu varṇyanāyakaviṣayatayā /
tvadaṅgeti /
tvadaṅgamārdavaṃ paśyataḥ sarvasyaiva citte mālatyādīnāṃ kaṭhoratāvabhāsata ityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: Here, in the non-contextual subjects <s>mālatī</s> etc., there is a connection through the quality of hardness.
He concludes <s>Tulyayogitā</s>: 'thus this...' etc.
<s>Tulyayogitā</s> should be recognized in contextual subjects or in others,
arising from the connection with a common quality or action, having a fitting meaning.

body.translated_text:
'When the similarity is implied' and 'through the referent level' — these two are governing conditions; the rest is the definition — he explains: 'without the use of <s>iva</s> (like) etc....' etc.
Contextual and non-contextual — these are the two domains.
Quality and action — these are the two types of property.
Therefore a fourfold classification should be noted:
In contextual subjects — connection through quality and connection through action.
In non-contextual subjects — likewise.
For <s>Tulyayogitā</s> is the connection through a common quality or action.
He reveals this etymology: '<s>anvitārtha</s>...' etc.
<s>Anvitārthā</s> means having a fitting meaning.
'<s>Sajja</s>' — the days are adorned with the rays (<s>ātapatrāṇi</s>) of parasol-like objects.
But the lotuses are adorned with the petals of well-born (<s>sujāta</s>) leaves.
'<s>Pāṭala</s>' in one sense means a color, in the other a flower.
He shows the contextual subject and the connection through action: 'here, in the description of the season...' etc.
The season is summer.
With contextual subjects, for the connection through quality, he says: 'likewise in quality too...' etc.
'<s>Yogapaṭṭa</s>' (yoga-belt) — here, due to the context of austerity, the yoga-belt etc. are contextual.
The quality of 'fitness' is connected in the form of attribution of quality-nature — if they are fit, then let it be said — through this challenge.
By this, the variety of attribution of presence or absence in quality and action is also indicated.
'The horse runs' — the dust that fell from the horse-army onto the face of the <s>Gūrjara</s> king was wiped by some compassionate slender lady.
But your fame — because of your swordsmanship.
He shows the non-contextual domain with connection through action: 'here, with respect to the <s>Gūrjara</s>...' etc.
By the reference 'by some lady' in relation to the <s>Gūrjara</s>, the lady's non-contextual nature is indicated.
But the swordsmanship, because it pertains to the hero being described.
'Your body' — seeing the softness of your limbs, in everyone's heart the <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine) and the like appear as hard — this is the meaning.

body.text:
atha saṅgatipuraskāreṇa dīpakaṃ prastauti-prastutāprastutayoḥ ityādi /
atha sūtram-
body.translated_text:
Now, with a preliminary connection, he introduces <s>Dīpaka</s> (illumination): 'of the contextual and non-contextual...' etc.
Now the <s>sūtra</s>:

body.text: prastutāprastutānāṃ tu dīpakam || 24 ||
body.translated_text: Of the contextual and non-contextual subjects, <s>Dīpaka</s> (illumination). || <s>RuAss</s> 24 ||

body.text:
samānadharmābhisaṃbandha ityanuṣajyate /
adhikāramanusmārayan vyacaṣṭe - opamyasyetyādinā /
iha prākaraṇikāḥ aprākaraṇikāścopādīyante /
teṣvekataratropāttaḥsādhāraṇo dharmo 'nyatropakaroti /
ato dīpanarūpādupakārāt dīpasadṛśo 'yamiti kṛtvā dīpakamidam /
tadidamuktam-prākaraṇikāprākaraṇiketyādinā /
aupamyasya gamyatvaṃ prāgvadevetyāha-tatrevādya prayogādityādi /
yaścātropamānopameyabhāvaḥ sa tulyayogitāto vilakṣaṇa ityāha-sa cetyādi /
vāstavaḥ prākaraṇikāprākaraṇikanimnatvāt /
pūrvatra tulyayogitāyām /
vaivakṣikaḥ vivakṣayā kḷtpaḥ /
vaivakṣikatvehetuḥ - śuddhaprākaraṇiketyādi /
śuddhaprākaraṇikatve hi upamānatvaṃ vāstavam /
śuddhāprākaraṇikatve tūpameyatvam /
tadidaṃ viśadīkaroti-prākaraṇikatvetyādinā /
nanu pratisvaṃ kriyāsambandhe kathaṃ padārthagataṃ ityata āha-anekasyaikakriyetyādi /
sambadhyamānadharmasyaikatvātpadārthatvopacaraṇamityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: Therefore, when it is truly at the sentence-meaning level, the threefold classification is justified — he says: 'in reality, however...' etc.
'<s>Rehai</s>' — [a Prakrit verse follows]:

children.text: rājate mihireṇa nabho rasena kāvyaṃḥ sareṇa yauvanam /
children.translated_text: The sky shines with the sun, poetry with <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic flavor), youth with beauty,
the ocean with nectar, and this world with you, O lord of men.

body.translated_text:
'Connection with a common property' is carried over from the previous rule.
Recalling the governing condition, he explains: 'of similarity...' etc.
Here, both contextual and non-contextual subjects are employed.
Among them, the common property employed for one side serves the other.
Therefore, because of the nature of illumination — service resembling a lamp — this is called <s>Dīpaka</s> (illumination).
This has been stated: 'contextual and non-contextual...' etc.
That the similarity is implied — as before — he says: 'there too, without the use of <s>iva</s>...' etc.
And the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> (standard-object of comparison) relationship here is different from <s>Tulyayogitā</s> — he says: 'and that...' etc.
It is real (<s>vāstava</s>) — because of the inherent subordination of contextual and non-contextual.
In the previous case, <s>Tulyayogitā</s> —
it is intentional (<s>vaivakṣika</s>), constructed by intention.
The reason for its being intentional: 'in purely contextual...' etc.
In pure contextuality, the <s>upamāna</s> status is real.
In pure non-contextuality, the <s>upameya</s> status.
He clarifies this: 'in contextuality...' etc.
Now, when there is a separate connection with action for each, how can it be at the referent level? — He answers: 'when many share one action...' etc.
Because of the oneness of the property being connected, the status of being at the referent level is figuratively attributed — this is the meaning.

body.text:
dhunī sariddhavaḥ patiḥ, sāgara ityarthaḥ /
idaṃ kriyāyāḥ ādivākyagatatvādādādidīpakam /
saṃcāreti /
nilayo gṛham astamayaśca /
pallavarāgo māṇikyaviśeṣaḥ yogāḍharāgaḥ(?) /
idamapyādidīpakam /
kriyāyāḥ prathama padatvam tantramiti dyotayitum-(yathā veti) /
(visamaao)iti /
etanmadhyadīpakam /

children.translated_text: '<s>Bole i</s>' — because the action is placed in the middle clause.
'<s>Kivaṇāṇa</s>' — [a Prakrit verse follows]:

children.text: kṛpaṇānāṃ dhanaṃ nāgānāṃ phaṇāmaṇiḥ kesarāṇi siṃhānām /
children.translated_text: The wealth of misers, the crest-jewels of serpents, the manes of lions,
and the breasts of chaste women — why are they touched by the dead?

body.translated_text:
<s>Dhunī</s> means 'river'; <s>dhava</s> means 'lord'; <s>pati</s> means the ocean — this is the meaning.
This is <s>Ādidīpaka</s> (initial illumination) because the action appears in the first clause.
'<s>Saṃcāra</s>' — <s>nilaya</s> means 'house' and also 'sunset.'
<s>Pallavarāga</s> is a particular type of ruby; <s>yogāḍharāga</s> (?)
This too is <s>Ādidīpaka</s>.
To indicate that the action being in the first word is the principle — (as in the example).
'<s>Visamāo</s>' — this is <s>Madhyadīpaka</s> (middle illumination).

body.text:
jīvitānna (jīvitāṃ na?) spṛśyante ityarthaḥ /
kriyādīpakatrayaṃ nigamayati-eva-meketi /
anayaivanītyā kārakadīpakaṃ udāhartumāha-atra ca yathetyādi /
sādhūnāmiti /

children.translated_text: He reveals the <s>Kārakadīpaka</s> character: 'here, because of the instrumental relation...' etc.
He says that <s>Mālādīpaka</s> (garland illumination) will appear in another context: 'in another aspect, however...' etc.
<s>Dīpaka</s> (illumination), having real similarity, is based on contextual and non-contextual subjects,
in initial, middle, and final clauses, differentiated by action and case-relation.

body.translated_text:
The meaning is: they are not touched by the living.
He concludes the threefold action-<s>Dīpaka</s>: 'thus one...' etc.
By this very method, to illustrate <s>Kārakadīpaka</s> (case-relation illumination), he says: 'and here, as...' etc.
'Of the good' —

body.text: atha vākyārthagatatvena prativastūpamāṃ sūtrayati-
body.translated_text: Now he formulates the <s>sūtra</s> on <s>Prativastūpamā</s> (counterpart simile), which operates at the sentence-meaning level:

body.text: vākyārthagatatvena sāmānyasya vākyadvaye pṛthaṅnirdeśa prativastūpamā || 25 ||
body.translated_text: When the common property, operating at the sentence-meaning level, is separately expressed in two sentences — that is <s>Prativastūpamā</s> (counterpart simile). || <s>RuAss</s> 25 ||

body.text:
saṅgatimāha-padārthārabveti /
iha nānālaṅkāra śaṅkāmapanetuṃ viṣayaṃ vibhajati-tatra sāmānyadharmasyetyādi /
ittā(ivā?)dikamupādāya sāmānyadharmasya sakṛnnirdeśa upamāyāmevodāhṛtaṃ 'prabhāmahatyāśikhayeva dīpa' iti /
ivādikamupādāyavastuprativastubhāvenāsakṛnnirdeśe 'pi saiva 'yāntyā muhurvalitakandharamānanaṃ tadāvṛtta vṛntaśatapatranibha'miti /
ivādikamanupādāya yathā sakṛnnirdeśastadā prastutāprastutānāṃ samastatve dīpakaṃ, tathaiva vyastatve tulyayogitā /
tadubhayamapi samanantarameva darśitam /
asakṛnnirdeśetu dvayī gatiḥ-śuddhasāmānyarūpatvaṃ, bimbapratibimbo vā /
śuddhasāmānyatvaṃ nāma sambandhibhedamātrāddharmasya pṛthaṅnirdeśaḥ /
tathā ivādyanupādāne prativastūpamā /
prativastūpamāṃnirvakti-vastuśabdasyetyādi /
vastuśabda iha vākyārthaparaḥ /
upamā tu sāmyam /
prativākyārthaṃ bhavatītyanvarthāśrayaṇā /
nanu yadi dharmasyāsakṛnnirdeśarūpaṃ śuddhasāmānyarūpatvaṃ tadā kiṃ paryāyāntareṇetyata āha-kevalaṃ kāvyetyādi /
uddeśapratinirdeśabhāvābhāve yadā tasyaiva punarupādānaṃ, tadā paryāyāntarābhāve anavīkṛtadoṣaḥ syāt /
ataḥ paryāyāntareṇa pṛthaṅnirdeśeḥ iti kāvyasamayaḥ /
so 'yaṃ prativastūpamāviṣayaḥ /
atha dharmyapekṣo bimbapratibimbabhāvo yadā, tadā dṛṣṭānto vakṣyata ityāha-dvitīyaprakāretyādi /
sādṛśyādhikāramanusmārayatitadevamaupamyetyādi /
cakorya iti /
āvantyaḥ avantīprabhavāḥ /
dharmasya śuddhasāmānyarūpatāṃ paryāyāntaratvaṃ ca darśayati-atra caturatvamityādi /

children.translated_text: He explains the further distinction (<s>vicchitti</s>): 'not merely...' etc.
For brevity, he shows the previous example itself [applied] with dissimilarity: '<s>Vināvantī</s>' (without), and so on.
Because of the repeated indication of the common property and the absence of connection [between the sentences] as in an <s>Ivādara</s> (simile-indicator),
it should be known as <s>Prativastūpamā</s> (Analogue-Simile), from the equivalence of meaning between the counter-sentences.

body.translated_text:
He explains the connection: 'beginning from the referent level...' etc.
Here, to remove the suspicion of various figures, he divides the domain: 'there, of the common property...' etc.
With the use of '<s>iva</s>' (like) etc., when the common property is expressed once, it has already been illustrated as <s>upamā</s> — as in 'her radiance, as if a flame of the lamp.'
With '<s>iva</s>' etc., even when expressed more than once through the relationship of object and counterpart — it is still the same <s>upamā</s> — as in 'her face, as she goes, with repeatedly turning neck, resembles a lotus with a bent stem.'
Without '<s>iva</s>' etc., when expressed once, if the contextual and non-contextual are combined — it is <s>Dīpaka</s> (illumination); if separated — it is <s>Tulyayogitā</s> (equal connection).
Both of these have just been illustrated.
But when expressed more than once, there are two possibilities: pure common-property form, or original-and-reflection form.
Pure common-property form means the separate expression of a property solely due to the difference of the related subjects.
Thus, without '<s>iva</s>' etc., it is <s>Prativastūpamā</s> (counterpart simile).
He explains <s>Prativastūpamā</s>: 'the word <s>vastu</s>...' etc.
The word <s>vastu</s> here refers to sentence-meaning.
<s>Upamā</s> means similarity.
It occurs for each sentence-meaning — thus the self-explanatory etymology.
Now, if the pure common-property form means expressing the property more than once, then why use a different synonym? — He answers: 'merely in poetry...' etc.
In the absence of an original-reference relationship, when the same property is taken up again, if a different synonym is not used, the fault of <s>anavīkṛta</s> (unrenewed [repetition]) would arise.
Therefore, the separate expression using a different synonym is the convention of poetry.
This is the domain of <s>Prativastūpamā</s>.
Now, when the original-and-reflection relationship depends on the qualified — then it will be stated as <s>Dṛṣṭānta</s> (example/illustration) — he says: 'in the second mode...' etc.
Recalling the governing topic of similarity: 'thus, similarity...' etc.
'<s>Cakorī</s>' — <s>Āvantyaḥ</s> means originating from <s>Avantī</s>.
He shows the pure common-property form and the use of different synonyms: 'here, cleverness...' etc.

body.text: atha dṛṣṭāntaṃ sūtrayati-
body.translated_text: Now he formulates the definition of <s>Dṛṣṭānta</s> (Illustrative Example):

body.text: tasyāpi bimbapratibimbatayā nirdeśe dṛṣṭāntaḥ || 26 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Dṛṣṭānta</s> (Illustrative Example) is when that [similarity] too is expressed in the manner of an image and its reflection (<s>Bimba-Pratibimba</s>). // <s>RuAss</s>_26 //

body.text:
vyācaṣṭe-tasyāpi na kevalamityādi /
prativastūpamānyāyena dvaividhyamāha-ayamapīti /
abdhirlaṅghita iti /
gurukulākliṣṭaḥ nityopāsanena tadekaśaraṇībhūtaḥ /
atra bahūnāṃ vānarabhaṭaiḥ manthācalena sahadharmyapekṣo bimbapratibimbabhāvaḥ /
divyavāgupāsanasya abdhilaṅghanena gurukliṣṭatvasyā pātālanimagratvena ca dharmāpekṣaḥ /
nanu jānāti jānīta iti jñānasya pṛthaṅnirdeśāt kathamidaṃ dṛṣṭāntodāharaṇamityata āha-atra yadyapītyādi /
naitannibandhanamiti /
na hi jñānanibandhanaṃ aupamyaṃ vivakṣitaṃ, jñānasyopacārāt /
yatra tu vivakṣā tatra na kiñcinnyūnamityata āha-yannibandhanaṃ cetyādi /
idaṃ sādharmye /
kṛtañceti /
tvayā manasi garvābhimukhe kṛte tatkṣaṇameva dviṣo nihatā ityarthaḥ /
dvau cakārau kriyayoreka rūpakālatāmāhaturyataḥ /
vaidharmyeṇa pratibimbanaṃ nidarśayati-atra nihitatvāderityādi /
nihatatvaṃ garvābhimukhīkaraṇaṃ ca anvayamukhena uktam /
tamaḥsthānaṃ udayādrimaulitvaṃ ca vyatirekamukhena /

children.translated_text: From the presentation 'as long as... not' (<s>Na yāvat</s>).
Therefore [there is] reflection through dissimilarity.
When the property and property-bearer are presented in the manner of image and counter-image (<s>Bimba-Anubimba</s>),
it should be known as the figure of <s>Dṛṣṭānta</s> (Illustrative Example), resting on the equivalence of separate sentence-meanings.

body.translated_text: He explains the connection: '<s>Pratibimba</s>' (reflection). He explains: 'Of that too, not merely,' and so on. He states the twofold division following the principle of <s>Prativastūpamā</s>: 'This one too.' '<s>Abdhir laṅghitaḥ</s>' (the ocean was crossed): '<s>Gurukula-akliṣṭaḥ</s>' means one who is devoted through constant attendance, having become wholly dependent on that [teacher]. Here, the image-reflection relation, with regard to the common property, holds between the many [qualities] — the monkey-warriors and the churning-mountain. The connection through common properties holds between the service of divine speech and the crossing of the ocean, and between devotion to the teacher and submersion in the netherworld. But since knowledge is separately indicated as 'he knows, they know' — how is this an example of <s>Dṛṣṭānta</s>? — to this he says: 'Here, although,' and so on. 'Not based on that' — for the similarity based on knowledge is not intended, since the [word] 'knowledge' is used figuratively. But where there is [such] intention, nothing is lacking — to this he says: 'And that which is the basis,' and so on. This [is an example] with similarity. '<s>Kṛtañca</s>' (and done): 'When you turned your mind toward pride, at that very instant the enemies were slain' — this is the meaning. The two uses of '<s>ca</s>' (and) indicate the simultaneity of the two actions. He shows the reflection through dissimilarity: 'Here, of being slain,' and so on. Being slain and the turning toward pride are stated by way of positive correlation (<s>Anvaya</s>). The place of darkness and the state of being the crest of the rising mountain are [stated] by way of negative correlation (<s>Vyatireka</s>).

body.text: nidarśanāṃ sūtrayati-
body.translated_text: He formulates the definition of <s>Nidarśanā</s> (Exemplification):

body.text: saṃbhavatāsaṃbhavatā vā vastusambandhena gamyamānaṃ pratibimbakaraṇaṃnidarśanā || 27 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Nidarśanā</s> (Exemplification) is the creation of a reflection (<s>Pratibimbakaraṇa</s>) that is understood through a connection of objects — whether possible or impossible. // <s>RuAss</s>_27 //

body.text:
saṅgatimāha-pratibimbeti /
vyācaṣṭe-tatra kvacidityādi /
vastusambandho vākyārthasambandhaḥ /
itthamiyaṃ dvidhā-sambhavadvastusambandhā, asambhavadvastusambandhāceti-cūḍāmaṇīti /
yo girirāgataṃ abhyāgataṃ raviṃ satāṃ ātitheyī atithisatkṛtiḥ kāryeti bodhayan dhatte /
yojayati-atra bodhayandhatta iti /
bo dhanasamarthasya ācārogirau prayiktaḥ tasyācetantve 'pi kārīṣo 'griradhyāpayatītivat giriḥ gṛhamedhino bodhanakriyāsamarthān karotīti tatsāmarthyācaraṇo ṇicaḥ prayogāt sambhavati vastusambandhaḥ /
avyātsa iti /
sa śivo 'vyādityarthaḥ /
yasyenduḥ smaracāpalīlāṃ spṛśati /
atrānyasambandhinyā līlāyā anyena sparśāsaṃbhavāt iyamasaṃbhavadvastusambandhā /
nanu tarhi asaṅgatireva syādityata āha-laulāsadṛśīṃ līlāmityādi /
lakṣaṇāśrayaṇādadūraviprakarṣam /
vaicitryāntarāyāha-eṣāpītyādi /
samanantaredāhṛtāyāmekakriyābhisambandhāt padārthavṛttitā /
tvatpādeti /
nakharatnānāṃ nisargaśoṇātvāt alakta(ka)mārjanameva pāṇḍurīkaraṇaṃ na bhavati yataḥ atra yeṣāṃ dṛṣṭāntadhīḥ te mandā ityāha-kecidityādi /
vākyārthanairapekṣye dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
sāpekṣatve tu nidarśanetyāha-yatra tu prakṛta ityādi /
sāmānādhikaraṇye nādhyaropyata iti vākyaikatāśrayaṇena ekakriyānvayāt prakṛtāntaḥ pātitvaṃ nīyata ityarthaḥ /
tatra vākye prakṛtāprakṛtavākyayoḥ sambandhānupapattimūlā nidarśanaivetyarthaḥ /
yatrāpyanatisphuṭaṃ sāpekṣatvaṃ dṛṣṭāntadhīrmābhūditi udāharaṇena darśayati-evaṃ caśuddhāntetyādi /
āśramavāsino janasya śuddhāntadurlabhaṃ vapuryadīti yacchrabda uttaravākye tarhidūrīkṛtā iti tacchrabda mutthāpayati iti vākyārthayoḥ sāpekṣatvānnidarśanaiva iyam /
tadetadāha-uktanyāyeneti /
atha vaicitryānyarāyāha-iyaṃ ca sāmānyainaivetyādi /
sāmānyena vākyārthayopasaṃbandhāt pratipādanaṃ vaicitryānataropoddhātaḥ /
vaicitryāntaraṃ vivecayati-upameyavṛttasyetyādi /
śuddhāntadurlabhamityādau hi upameyavṛtte 'dhyāropitasya upamānavṛttasyāmbhavaḥ /
athaitadviparyayo 'pi - viyoga iti /
viyogena nimittena pāṇḍarībhūtānāṃ nārīṇāṃ gaṇḍataleyaḥ pāṇḍimāsakharjurī mañjarīgarbhareṇuṣvalakṣyatetyatra upameyavṛttasya gaṇḍapāṇḍimro mañjarīgarbhareṇurūpa upamānavṛtterlakṣyatvāsaṃbhavāt upamā pratīyate /
tadetadāha-atra gaṇḍatalamityādi /

children.text: asyaiva ca prakārasya vaicitryāntarāyāha-eṣa prakāra upameyavṛttasya upamānavṛtte 'nvayāsaṃbhavalakṣaṇām /
children.translated_text: He mentions another variety of this very type: 'This type [involves] the impossibility of the connection of the subject-of-comparison occurrence with the standard-of-comparison occurrence.'
'<s>Muṇḍasira</s>' (shaved-head) —
'On the shaved head, you hold a <s>Badara</s> fruit; upon the <s>Badara</s>, another <s>Badara</s>, placed firmly.
You make yourself twice as tall — the fool! The clever ones lead [him] astray.'

body.translated_text: He states the connection: '<s>Pratibimba</s>' (reflection). He explains: 'There, in some cases,' and so on. Object-connection (<s>Vastusambandha</s>) means connection of sentence-meanings. Thus this is twofold: with a possible object-connection and with an impossible object-connection. '<s>Cūḍāmaṇi</s>' — 'the mountain, conveying [the idea] that the arrived sun, which has come, should be honored as a guest of the virtuous, holds [it].' He glosses: 'Here, conveying and holding.' The conduct [attributed to the mountain], which is capable of conveying [a message], is applied to the mountain; even though it is inanimate, just as 'the fire of dried cowdung teaches' — the mountain makes the householders capable of the act of conveying — from the usage of the causative expressing that capacity, the object-connection is possible. '<s>Avyāt</s>' (may he protect): 'May that <s>Śiva</s> protect' — this is the meaning. Whose moon touches the playful sport of <s>Smara</s> (the Love-god). Here, since the sport belonging to one [being] cannot be touched by another, this has an impossible object-connection. But then, would this not simply be incoherence? — to this he says: 'A sport resembling playfulness,' and so on. Through recourse to <s>Lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification), [the distance is] not far-fetched. He mentions another variety: 'This too,' and so on. In the example just cited, from the connection with a single action, there is a word-level occurrence. '<s>Tvatpāda</s>' (your foot): since the nail-jewels are naturally red, the application of lac is itself a whitening — because [it makes them appear white by contrast]. Here, those who see [this as] <s>Dṛṣṭānta</s> are dull-witted — he says: 'Some,' and so on. When there is independence of sentence-meanings, it is <s>Dṛṣṭānta</s>. When there is dependence, it is <s>Nidarśanā</s> — he says: 'But where the subject matter,' and so on. Through taking recourse to sentence-unity by co-predication, from the connection with a single action, the subject matter is brought within [the scope of a single utterance] — this is the meaning. In that sentence, from the impossibility of connection between the sentence concerning the subject and the sentence concerning the non-subject, it is necessarily <s>Nidarśanā</s>. Even where the dependence is not very clear, lest the notion of <s>Dṛṣṭānta</s> arise, he shows with an example: 'Thus, of the pure inner quarters,' and so on. Of the forest-dwelling person, 'if [this person has] a body difficult to obtain in the inner quarters (<s>Śuddhānta</s>)' — the word 'if' (<s>yad</s>) in the latter sentence generates the word 'then' (<s>tat</s>) in '[then] she has been kept away.' Since the sentence-meanings are mutually dependent, this is <s>Nidarśanā</s>. He states this: 'By the stated principle,' and so on. Now he mentions another variety: 'And this, in general,' and so on. Through the general connection of sentence-meanings, the exposition [forms] an introduction to another variety. He analyzes another variety: 'Of the object-of-comparison occurrence,' and so on. In '<s>Śuddhāntadurlabham</s>' (difficult to obtain in the inner quarters) and so on, the occurrence of the standard-of-comparison applied onto the subject-of-comparison occurrence is impossible [literally]. And the reverse of this is also [possible]: '<s>Viyoga</s>' (separation). The pallor of the cheeks of women who have become pale from the cause of separation is perceived in the pollen within the buds of the <s>Kharjūra</s> palm flowers — here, the impossibility of the occurrence of the subject-of-comparison (cheek-pallor) being perceived in the standard-of-comparison occurrence (bud-pollen) gives rise to a suggested simile. He states this: 'Here, the surface of the cheek,' and so on.

body.text:
chrekā vidagdhāḥ /
chralyante chalaṃ nīyante /
atra chrekachralanahetornaṣphaladuḥsaṅghaṭamūḍhakāryaparamparālakṣaṇasya pratīyamānasya upameyavṛttasya badaradharaṇādāvupamānavṛtte 'nvayāsaṃbhavaḥ /
sa ca parasparasavyapekṣata(yā)paḍktyavasthānat śṛṅkhalānyāyena sthitaḥ /
mitho 'napekṣapaḍktyavasthānalakṣaṇāyā mālārūpeṇāpi saṃbhavatītyāha-iyamapīti /
apiśabdo bhinnakramaḥ /
mālayāpi bhavantītyarthaḥ /
araṇyeti araṇyaruditaṃ kṛtaṃ tādṛśoduḥkhātibhārasya duḥkhabhāgijanamantareṇa anubhūtatvāt /
śavaśarīramudvartitaṃ agarucandanā dinānulitpam /
tathāvidhasya saṃskārasya tasya vā svasya vā anyeṣāṃ vā bhogāyogāt /
sthale 'bjamavaropitaṃ bhuvanalālanīyasya vastuno 'patvāt /
suciramiti prativākyamanvīyate /
ūṣare varṣitaṃ nairarthakyanaiṣphalyayorudvelatvāt /
ścapucchramavanāmitaṃ cirasaṃskārādhāne 'pya nāhitaṃsaṃskāratvāt /
badhirakarṇajāpaḥ kṛtaḥ /
jāpaḥ upāṃśurahasyoktiḥ /
apātramiti jñātvaiva durutkaṇṭhayā samārambhāt /
andhamukhamaṇḍanā kṛtā tasya anupayogādanyeṣāṃ viḍambanāspadatvāt /
abudho janaḥ sevito yaditi vākyārthena viśeṣito yacchabdaḥ pradhāna vākyārthabhūtā(m) kriyā (mu)pagṛhṇāti /
yadabudhajanasevanaṃ tadaraṇyaruditādikaraṇāmityupameyavṛttasya upamānavṛtte 'dhyāropitasya anvayāsaṃbhavo mālayāvatiṣṭhate /
atha śābdopādānāṃ vināpi arthākṣepādeva nidarśanāvaicitryaṃ bhavatītyāha-kvacitpunarityādi /
niṣedho hi prātpipūrvaka eveti prātpimākṣipati /
niṣedhākṣitpāyāḥ prāpteḥ samvandhānuvapapattirapi kvacinnidarśanābījamityarthaḥ /
tadā(nī miya)mārthīti bhāvaḥ /
utkopa iti /
atra padbhyāṃ haṃsagatirmukteti tyāgarūpaniṣedhabalāt pādayorhasagatiprātpirākṣitpā /

children.translated_text: Being unable to directly connect [with the feet], it conveys similarity.
He states this: 'Here, "released,"' and so on.
Whether the object-connection is possible or impossible, if it conveys
a reflection, then it should be recognized as <s>Nidarśanā</s> (Exemplification).

body.translated_text: '<s>Chrekā</s>' means the clever ones. '<s>Chralyante</s>' means they are led astray [deceived]. Here, the suggested meaning — characterized by the chain of foolish actions involving the ill-fitting combination of <s>Naṣphala</s> (a worthless fruit) [with a shaved head] — as the subject-of-comparison occurrence, its connection in the standard-of-comparison occurrence of holding the <s>Badara</s> and so on is impossible. And this [impossibility] stands in the manner of a chain, from the mutual interdependence in the sequential arrangement. He says it is also possible in the form of a garland, characterized by a sequential arrangement without mutual dependence: 'This too,' and so on. The word '<s>api</s>' (also) indicates a different order. 'Also in the form of a garland' — this is the meaning. '<s>Araṇya</s>' (wilderness): 'Weeping in the wilderness was done' — because such excessive sorrow was experienced without anyone to share in the suffering. 'Anointed on a corpse' — smeared with sandalwood, <s>Agaru</s>, and such [fragrant substances]. Because such ceremonial preparation is useless to it, or to oneself, or to others. 'A lotus planted on dry land' — because [this involves] the degradation of an object that the whole world cherishes. '<s>Suciram</s>' (for a long time) is connected with each counter-sentence. 'Rained upon barren salt-land' — because of the excess of purposelessness and fruitlessness. 'A dog's tail bent down' — because even after prolonged effort at training, the training is not retained. 'Whispering into a deaf ear was done' — <s>Jāpa</s> means a whispered secret utterance. '<s>Apātram</s>' (unworthy vessel): because the effort was begun out of irresistible longing even knowing [the recipient to be unworthy]. 'Adorning a blind face was done' — because of its uselessness to [the blind person] and its being an object of mockery to others. 'An ignorant person was served' — the word 'which' (<s>yad</s>), qualified by the sentence-meaning, takes up the main predicate as its principal clause: 'That serving of an ignorant person is [equivalent to] weeping in the wilderness and such' — the impossibility of connection of the subject-of-comparison occurrence with the standard-of-comparison occurrence stands in the form of a garland. Now, even without explicit verbal indicators, the variety of <s>Nidarśanā</s> can arise from mere implication of meaning — he says: 'Sometimes, however,' and so on. For prohibition presupposes [a prior] possibility; so the prohibition implies the possibility. The impossibility of connection arising from the possibility implied by the prohibition is also sometimes the seed of <s>Nidarśanā</s>. In that case, 'this is [based on] meaning' — this is the purport. '<s>Utkopa</s>' (agitation): here, 'the gait of swans has been released from the feet' — by the force of the prohibition in the form of relinquishment, the possibility of the swan-gait belonging to the feet is implied.

children.translated_text: When two sentences [serve] as image and counter-image and are connected to the subject matter,
if they are independent [of each other], it is <s>Dṛṣṭānta</s> (Illustrative Example); if mutually dependent, it is <s>Nidarśanā</s> (Exemplification).

body.text:
itthamabhedaprādhānyādhikāranipātino 'laṅkārāḥ vivecitāḥ /
atha bhedaprādhānyena vyatirekaṃ sūtrayati-
body.translated_text: Thus the figures falling under the heading of predominance of non-difference have been analyzed. Now he formulates the definition of <s>Vyatireka</s> (Contrast) with the predominance of difference:

body.text: bhedaprādhānye upamānādupameyasyādhikye viparyaye vā vyatirekaḥ || 28 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Vyatireka</s> (Contrast) is [the figure obtained] when, with the predominance of difference, the object of comparison (<s>Upameya</s>) exceeds the standard of comparison (<s>Upamāna</s>), or the reverse. // <s>RuAss</s>_28 //

body.text:
bhedaprādhānye sādharmya ityanuṣajyate /
bhedaprādhānyaṃ vyatirekasyoktacaramanusmārayan adhikaroti - adhunetyādi /
bhedamasambhavavaicitryadvayaṃ prabhedabījatvena uṭghāṭayati-bhedo vailakṣaṇyamityādi /
viparyayaśabdāt mithyājñānabhramo mā bhūdityāha-viparyayo nyūnaguṇatvamiti /
diddakṣava iti /
atra nīlotpalinī vikāsāpekṣayākṣisahasrapakṣmalatāyā adhikaguṇatvam /
kṣīṇaḥ kṣīṇo 'pīti /

children.text: atra anivartino yauvanasya kṣayiṇo 'pi bhūyo 'bhivardhitaśaśivyapekṣayā nyūnaguṇatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, youth — though non-returning and waning — has lesser qualities compared to the moon, which waxes again even after waning.
He connects both [examples]: 'Here, with the blossoming one,' and so on.
<s>Vyatireka</s> (Contrast) is established when difference predominates in similarity,
either from the superiority of the object of comparison (<s>Upameya</s>) or from the inferiority compared to the standard of comparison (<s>Upamāna</s>).

body.translated_text: 'With the predominance of difference in [regard to] similarity' — this is carried over [from the preceding]. He introduces the predominance of difference as the [defining feature] of <s>Vyatireka</s> by recalling what was already stated: 'Now,' and so on. He reveals the twofold division — through difference and through the variety of impossibility — as the seed of sub-types: 'Difference means distinctiveness,' and so on. Lest there be error or false understanding from the word '<s>Viparyaya</s>' (reverse), he says: '<s>Viparyaya</s> means possessing lesser qualities.' '<s>Diddakṣavaḥ</s>' (desirous of seeing): here, with respect to blooming, the thousand-eyelashed [eye] has superior qualities compared to the blue lotus (<s>Nīlotpalinī</s>). '<s>Kṣīṇaḥ kṣīṇo 'pi</s>' (waning, even though waning):

body.text: sarhektiṃ sūtrayati-
body.translated_text: He formulates the definition of <s>Sahokti</s> (Co-statement):

body.text: upamānopameyayorekasya prādhānyanirdeśe 'parasya sahārthasambandhe sahoktiḥ || 29 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Sahokti</s> (Co-statement) is when, in the statement of the primacy of one of the standard of comparison and the object of comparison, the other is connected through the meaning of 'together with' (<s>Saha</s>). // <s>RuAss</s>_29 //

body.text:
adhikāramanusmārayan sāmagrīmasyā vivinakti-bhedaprādhānya ityevetyādinā /
nanu sahārtha tayā tulyakakṣyayoḥ kathaṃ bhedapradhānatetyata āha-guṇapradhānabhāvetyādi /
satyam /
sahārthasāmarthyāt sādharmyamevātra /
bhedaprādhānyaṃ tu vyatirekanayena sādhārmyabhitti kamiha na bhavati api tu guṇā pradhānabhāvabhittikamiti yāvat /
nanu samānayogatve guṇaprādhānabhāvo 'pi kīdṛgītyata āha-sahārthaprakteti /
sahārtho hi tṛtīyāṃ taṃ guṇatvena prayojayati /
nanu sahārthatve ka upamānopameyabhāva ityata āha-upamānopameyatvaṃ cetyādi /
taddhi tṛtīyāntasya viśeṣaṇatvādupamānatvaṃ vivakṣyate /
itarasya tu viśeṣyatvādupameyatvam /
ato vaivakṣikameva na tu vāstavamiti bhāvaḥ /
avāstatatve hetumāha-dvayorapītyādi /
nanu dvayoḥ prākaraṇikatvamevāprākaraṇikatvameva vetikiṃ niyāmakamityata āha-sahārthasāmarthyāditi /
nanu tarhi vaivakṣikatve katarat kena rūpeṇa vivakṣyatāmityata āha-tṛtīyāntasyetyādi /
nanu pradhānamapi tṛtīyāntena nirdeśamarhatītyata āha-śābdaśceti /
sahaśabdo hi niyamena tṛtīyāntasya śābdaguṇatvaṃ kalpayati /
itarasya tu prādhānyam /
tarhi arthāpekṣayā kā sthitirityata āha-vastutastviti /
guṇasyāpi prādhānyaṃ, pradhānasyāpi guṇatvaṃ viparyayaḥ /
apiśabdādanavasthitirapi /
evaṃ nyāyakrame sthite 'pi viśeṣo 'nyo 'syāḥ prayojaka ityāha-tatrāpītyādi /
atiśayoktirapi na sākalyena asyā mūlamityata āha-sā cetyādi /
kāryakāraṇapratiniyamaviparyayo 'tra tulyakālatā na tu kāryasya pūrvakālatā sahārthatvāt /
abhedādhyavasāyastu dvidhā bhavatītyāha-abhedādhyavasāyaścetyādi /
teneyaṃ trividhopakṣitpā /
vaicitryāntaramupakṣipati-sāhityaṃ cātryetyādi /
kartṛkarmādi sāhityanibandhanenāpi prābhedena prathata iti yāvat /
krameṇodāharaṇāni /
bhavadaparādhairiti- atrāparādhānāṃ tṛtīyāntatvādguṇatā /
santāpasya prathamāntatvātpradhānatā /
ato guṇapradhānabhāva nibandhanaivātra bhedapradhānatā, na punarvṛddhikriyānibandhanā /
sa ca guṇapradhānabhāvaḥ sahārthaprayuktaḥ /
dvayośca prākaraṇikatvādupamānopameyabhāvo vaivakṣikaḥ /
aparādhānāṃ ca tṛtīyāntatvāt viśeṣaṇānāmupamānatvaṃ niyatamaparādhā yathā vardhanta iti /
santāpasya tu pradhānatvādupameyatvaṃ santāpastathā vardhata iti /
sa cāyaṃ guṇapradhānabhāvaḥ śābdaḥ /
arthaṃ vyapekṣya tu santāpa eva (iva)aparādhā vardhanta ityapi prāpteḥ /
nyāya kramo 'yaṃ udāharaṇāntareṣvapi yojanīyaḥ /
atra kāryakāraṇasamakālatvalakṣaṇātiśayoktirmulamiti darśayati-atrāparādhānāmityādi /
astaṃ bhāsvāniti-saṃhriyantāṃ viprakīrṇāni ekīkriyantāmityarthaḥ atra śleṣābhittikābhedādhyavasāyarūpā mūlamiti darśayati-atrāstaṅgamanamityādi /
astam ekadā giriḥ anyadātvavasāda ityubhayārthatvam /
kumudadalairiti-atra punaḥ aśleṣabhittikābhedādhyavasāyarūpamūlamiti darśayati-atra vighaṭanamityādi /
evamatiśayoktimūlatvādilakṣaṇo yo viśeṣaḥ tadabhāve sahoktimātraṃ nālaṅkāra iti vyutpādayati-etadviśeṣeti /
pratyudāharati-anena sārdhamiti /
kartṛsāhityalakṣaṇaṃ vaicitryamapyeṣveva darśitamityāha-etānyeveti /
eṣu hi santāpāparādhādi kartṛsāhityam-dyujana iti /
dyujanā devāḥ /
dyujanasya mṛtyunā saha manorathāvātpiḥ daityabalakṣayaḥ /
atra karmasāhityaṃ darśayati-atra karotikriyetyādi /
dyujanamṛtyoḥ ātpikriyāpekṣayā kartṛtve 'pi tasyopasarjanatvāt neha kartṛsāhityam /
yā tu (cakra iti)pradhānabhūtā karotikriyā tadapekṣayā karmatvātkarmasāhityametaditi yāvat /
evaṃ karaṇādisāhityavaicitryamunneyam /
atha punarvaicitryāyāha-iyaṃ ceti /
utprekṣitpamiti /
dhanuṣa utkṣepaḥ jyāvandhasaṅghaṭṭanam /
āsphālanamākarṣaḥ /
śilīmukhamokṣa ityādi kramikāṇi dhānuṣkakarmāṇi /
tatrā karṣaṇamātrāntaṃ paripaṇānāttāvantyevopavarṇitāni /
tatrātivatsalasya kauśikasya pulakānāṃ dhanurutkṣepasama samayamutkṣepaḥ, matsaragrastatvāt utkṣepamātrā paritoṣitānāṃ bhūpānāṃ dhanurnati(sama)samayaṃ mukhanatiḥ /
paripaṇatākarṣaṇasya janakasya natyantaṃ saṃśayānuvṛtteḥ /
jyāsphālanasamasamayaṃ saṃśayabuddhyāsphānam /
vaidehyāḥ punaḥ paripaṇanasiddhyantamanākṛṣṭamanaḥsamākarṣasamasama(yaṃ)ma(naḥ)samākarṣaḥ /

children.text: bhārgavāhaṅkṛtikandalasya tu dhanurbhaṅgāntamabhagrasya bhaṅgasamasamayaṃ bhaṅgaḥśrīmatā rāmacandreṇākārīti samanvayāt karmasāhityamiha mālātvenāvatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: Because of the syntactic connection that the breaking of <s>Bhārgava</s>'s bow, which was a sprout of his arrogance, was done simultaneously with the breaking by the illustrious <s>Rāmacandra</s>, it is a case of simultaneous occurrence.
Other cases too should be understood in the same manner as a series.
The subordinate-principal relation that is verbal—by that, the predominance of difference is prominent.
<s>Sahokti</s> (concurrent expression) is understood as embodying simultaneity and as dependent on <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole).

body.translated_text: Reminding of the governing rule, he analyzes the factors of this figure: '<s>bhedaprādhānya ityeva</s>' etc. Now, when there is equal status through the sense of accompaniment (<s>sahārtha</s>), how can there be predominance of difference?—to address this he says '<s>guṇapradhānabhāva</s>' etc. True, by the force of the meaning of accompaniment, what is here is indeed similarity. But the predominance of difference is not based on the principle of <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast)—the foundation of similarity does not apply here; rather, it is based on the relation of subordinate and principal (<s>guṇa-pradhāna</s>)—such is the purport. Now, in equal conjunction, what kind of subordinate-principal relation is there?—to address this he says '<s>sahārthaprakṛta</s>' etc. For the sense of accompaniment causes the instrumental-case term to function as subordinate. Now, when there is the sense of accompaniment, what constitutes the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> (standard-object of comparison) relation?—to address this he says '<s>upamānopameyatvaṃ ca</s>' etc. Because the instrumental-case term functions as a qualifier, its <s>upamāna</s> status is intended. The other, being the qualified, has <s>upameya</s> status. Therefore, this is merely intentional, not factual—such is the implied sense. He gives the reason for its non-factuality: '<s>dvayorapi</s>' etc. Now, what determines that both are contextual or both non-contextual?—to address this he says '<s>sahārthasāmarthyāt</s>' etc. Now, if it is intentional, which is intended as what?—to address this he says '<s>tṛtīyāntasya</s>' etc. Now, even the principal can be denoted by the instrumental case—to address this he says '<s>śābdaśca</s>' etc. For the word '<s>saha</s>' (with) necessarily constructs the verbal subordination of the instrumental-case term. The other has principality. Then what is the state of affairs with respect to the meaning?—to address this he says '<s>vastutas tu</s>' etc. Even the subordinate can be principal, and the principal can be subordinate—a reversal. By the word '<s>api</s>' (also), there is even instability. Even though this is the state of logical reasoning, another particular feature is the motivating factor of this figure—he says '<s>tatrāpi</s>' etc. <s>Atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is also not entirely the root of this figure—to address this he says '<s>sā ca</s>' etc. The reversal of the fixed correlation of cause and effect is here simultaneity, not the temporal priority of the effect—because of the sense of accompaniment. And the determination of non-difference is of two kinds—he says '<s>abhedādhyavasāyaśca</s>' etc. Thus this is presented as threefold. He presents another variety: '<s>sāhityaṃ cātra</s>' etc.—through the connection of agent, object, etc., it is also manifested in subtypes—such is the purport. Examples in order. '<s>Bhavadaparādhair</s>'—here, because the offenses are in the instrumental case, they are subordinate; because the torment is in the nominative case, it is principal. Therefore the predominance of difference here is founded on the subordinate-principal relation, not on the relation of growth and action.

body.text:
atha vinoktyau saṅgatimāha-sahoktipratibhaṭetyādi-pratibhaṭabhūtāṃ pratiyogibhūtām /
tatra sūtram-
body.translated_text: Now he establishes the connection with <s>vinokti</s> (expression of absence): '<s>sahoktipratibhaṭa</s>' etc.—'the counterpart of <s>sahokti</s>.' There the sūtra states—

body.text: vinā kañcidanyasya sadasattvābhāvo vinoktiḥ || 30 ||
body.translated_text: When in the absence of one thing, the existence or non-existence of another is stated, that is <s>vinokti</s> (expression of absence). (RuAss 30)

body.text:
vyācaṣṭesattvasyetyā(di) /
(vyatyayenābhāvaśabdārthau)pratyekamabhisambadhyete /
śobhanatvābhāvo 'śobhanatvaṃ tattvābhāvaḥ śobhanatvamiti /
kañcidarthaṃ vinā yatra śobhanatvaṃ nāsti saikā vinoktaḥ /
yatra tvaśobhanatvaṃ nāsti sānyeti dvirūpeyamityarthaḥ /
nanu kasmiṃścit tattvāsatve ityetāvataiva paryātpau (kiṃ?)niṣedhadvayāśrayaṇagauraveṇotyata āha-atra cetyādi /
anyanivṛttiprayukteti /
anyanivṛttiścet sadasattvanivṛttiṃ na prayojayati /

na hyasmin sati tattvamasattvaṃvetyuktau vicchittiḥ kācit /
ato 'nyanivṛttiprayuktā sadasattvanivṛttireva vinoktyalaṅkāraḥ iti bhāvaḥ /
asminsati sattvamasattvaṃ ceti vastuvidhiḥ , sattvalaṅkāraphalatvena prātpe prakāśyata ityāha-evaṃ cānyanivṛttāvapi ityādi /
dvirūpāyā api paripāṭyodāharaṇaṃ - vinayeti /
atra vinayaśaśisatkatvanivṛttyā śrīniśāvidagdhā (dhatā)ni vṛttiriti sattvābhāvodāharaṇam /
vinayādiṣu ca satsu śrīprabhṛtisadbhāvaḥ phalatvena prakāśyate /
tadidamabhisandhāyāha-atra vinayādītyādi /
vinādi śabdābhāve tadarthaṃ sadbhāve vinoktireveti vyutpādayitumāha-atra vinā śabda ityādi /
yathā sahoktāviti /
sahoktāvapyayaṃ nyāya iti yāvat /
atrodāharati-nirarthakaṃ janmeti /

ato vinoktiḥ iyam /
vināśabdānupādāne tvārthīti viśeṣaḥ /
tadidamabhisandhāyāha-ityādau vinoktirevetyādi /

udāhṛtaviṣaya iti /
nirarthakaṃ janmetyayamudāhṛto viṣayaḥ /

loke hi mṛgalocanāṃ vinā vicitravyavahārapratibhāprāgalbhyaṃ nāsti suhṛdā vinā ca sundarāśayatvam /

asattvā bhāvaṃ darśayati-atrāśobhanatvābhāvādityādi /

children.translated_text: Brilliance of imagination and beauty of conception are the two meanings of the word '<s>śobhana</s>' (beautiful).
He concludes: 'this is twofold'—thus.
If the cessation of existence or goodness of another is stated,
then <s>vinokti</s> is twofold; the twofold distinction here lies in the result.

body.translated_text: He explains: '<s>sattvasya</s>' etc. (By inversion, the meanings of the words 'existence' and 'absence' are connected to each respectively.) The absence of goodness is ungoodness; the absence of existence is non-existence. Thus <s>vinokti</s> is twofold: based on the absence of goodness and based on the absence of existence. He explains: '<s>prathama</s>' etc. In the first—'without you, the lotus-garden is not beautiful'—goodness is denied; not existence. In the second—'without you, spring does not exist here'—existence itself is denied. To show the difference between the two in terms of delight, he says '<s>tatra</s>' etc. The difference of the twofold distinction lies in the result—he explains: '<s>prathama</s>' etc. In the first, the purpose is the praise of the separated person through the indication of the ungoodliness of the thing. In the second, the purpose is the praise of the separated person through the indication of the non-existence of the thing. Thus in both cases, the praise of the separated person is common; but the means differs—through ungoodliness or non-existence. And the latter is more forceful because it implies the former—he says '<s>gauravāt</s>' etc. Now he shows how this is an <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure) and not a mere factual statement—he says '<s>nanu</s>' etc. True, the lotus-garden exists even without the beloved. But because it is as good as non-existent without her, the statement of its non-existence is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole). By the force of <s>atiśayokti</s>, <s>vinokti</s> is established as a figure.

body.text:
atha viśeṣaṇavicchittimūlau samāsoktiparikarau prastauti - adhunā viśeṣaṇeti /
viśeṣaṇa vicchittiśca dvirūpā sābhyaṃ sābhiprāyatā ca /
sāmye samāsoktimadhikaroti-tatrādāvityādi /
tatra sūtram /
body.translated_text: Now he introduces <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) and <s>parikara</s> (attendant expression), which are rooted in the delight of qualifiers: '<s>adhunā viśeṣaṇa</s>' etc. The delight of qualifiers is of two kinds: with inner connection (<s>sābhya</s>) and with external connection (<s>sābhya</s>)—

body.text: viśeṣeṇasāmyādaprastutasya gamyatve samāsoktiḥ || 31 ||
body.translated_text: When the irrelevant is understood through the similarity of qualifiers, that is <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression). (RuAss 31)

body.text:
yatra viśeṣyāṃśe prakṛtamātraparatā viśeṣaṇasāmyāt punaraprakṛto 'vagamyate sā samāsena saṃkṣepeṇā abhidhānāt samāsoktiḥ /
tadetadvyācikhyāsurviṣayavibhāgāyāha-iha prastutetyādi /
kvacidvācyatvam /
ubhayeṣāmiti śeṣaḥ /
kvacidgamyatvaṃ, ekatareṣāmita śeṣaḥ /
śleṣanirdeṣabhgyeti /
viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyāṃśayoḥ śleṣoranibandhane netyarthaḥ /
pṛthagupādānena viti /
viśeṣaṇāṃśe pṛthak śabdopādānenetyarthaḥ /
etaddvibhedamapi vācyatvaṃ śleṣālaṅkārasya viṣayaḥ /
yadā purgamyatvaṃ prastutaviṣayaṃ viśeṣaṇasāmyāt tadānīma prastutapraśaṃsā, yadā tvaprastutaviṣayaṃ tadā samāsoktiriti vivekaḥ /
aprastutasya gamyatve yadi viśeṣyasyāpi sāmyaṃ tadā kiṃ syādityata āha-viśeṣyasyāpi sāmye śleṣaprāpteriti /
śleṣamūladhvaniprātperiti yāvat /
nanu śleṣālaṅkāraḥ śabdaśaktimūladhvaniśceti triṣu viṣayeṣvapyasti śliṣṭapadāpanibandhaḥ /
tatra yadā śleṣaḥ tadārthadvayasya niyamena vācyatā /
vācyatvaṃ caivaṃ saṃbhavati-yadārthau dvāvapi prākaraṇikau staḥ aprākaraṇikau vā tadā viṣeṣaṇaviṣyāṃśayordvayorapi śliṣṭapadopanibandhāt śleṣālaṅkāraḥ /
abhidhāyā aniyantraṇāt dvāvapyarthau vācyau /
atha yadaikasya prākaraṇikatvamitarasya aprākaraṇikatvaṃ tadā viśeṣyāṃśe pṛthak śabdopādānabalādeva śleṣālaṅkāraḥ /
yadi viśeṣyāṃśe 'pi śliṣṭapadopanibandhaḥ tadā prakaraṇaniyantritāyā abhidhāyāḥ prākaraṇikārthaḥ evopakṣayāda prākaraṇikarthāvagatirvyañjanasyaiva viṣayaḥsyāt /
yadasamāsoktistadā /
viśeṣaṇāṃśe arthadvayapratipādakaśabdopanibandhaḥ viśeṣyāṃśe tu prākaraṇikārthamātraparatā /
tadā viśeṣaṇasāmyādaprastutasya gamyatvāduktalakṣaṇā samāsoktiḥ /
yadā punaḥ prākaraṇikāprākaraṇikayoḥ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyāṃśe 'pi śliṣṭatā tadā tāvanna samāsoktiḥ viśeṣaṇamātrasāmyalakṣaṇā yataḥ śleṣālaṅkāratvaprātpirapi /
katham? tatrārthadvayasya vācyataiva lakṣaṇaṃ yataḥ, na hyatra dvayorvācyatopapattiḥ prakaraṇapakṣapātinyā abhidhāyā aprākaraṇiker'the sparśābhāvāt aprākaraṇikasya samanvayasamanantara pratītikatvāt śabdaśaktimūlasya dhvaneḥ śleṣeṇa viṣayagrāsaprasaṅgācca /
vivikto 'yaṃ ghaṇṭāpathaḥ dhvaninidarśanarahasyavidāmityalam /
atha samāsoktirūpakayoḥ vaidharmyaṃ vivecayati-viśeṣaṇasāmyavaśādityādinā /
hirhetau /
yato viśeṣaṇasāmyādaprastutor'thaḥ pratīyate, ato viśeṣyāṃśe saṃsparśābhāvādviśeṣyaṃ prakṛtārthaṃ na svena rūpeṇa rūpavantaṃ kartumīṣṭe kindu viśeṣaṇāṃśapratītaṃ svavyavahāraṃ viśeṣaṇāṃśapratīte prakṛtārthavyavahāre 'vacchredakatvena samāropayati /
